#1721. Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as new signing confirmed

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Teenage defender Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham after leaving rivals West Ham in the summer.

In August, reports claimed that Spurs had beaten Arsenal to Allen’s signature, and the 15-year-old has now announced the move on social media.

The England U15s captain wrote in a post on Instagram: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”

Allen, who can operate either at centre-back or in defensive midfield, is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in England and his arrival continues Spurs’ busy youth recruitment strategy.

During last month’s Fan Advisory Board (FAB) meeting, the club confirmed that as part of their commitment to the academy, they had actively recruited players aged 16 and under and invested in the U10 to U17 age groups.

Allen is the latest highly-rated teenage talent to arrive at Hotspur Way, with Cole Ramsey (19), Kwasi Senyah (16), Gabriel Rigg (15) and Jake Maloney (14) all signing in recent months.

Tottenham are understood to be pairing football development with private schooling and strong professional terms once players turn 17, to beat competition from rival clubs.

The change in approach has been brought on by an acknowledgement internally that Spurs have struggled not only to offer academy players a pathway into the first team, but also to maximise their value by selling them on if they don’t believe they have a future at the club.

Tottenham hope to highlight the progression of 18-year-old winger Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut in the Premier League against Ipswich last weekend before being handed a new long-term contract, as an example of the pathway into the first team.

Meanwhile, the success of the current Championship leading goalscorer Will Lankshear, who joined Middlesbrough in a deal worth up to £20million in the summer, showcases Spurs’ willingness to find productive permanent solutions for players who can’t be guaranteed regular first-team minutes after coming through the academy.

#1720. ‘Apology FC’: Manchester United fans make clear demand after Sporting referee ‘robbery’

Manchester United fans have it out at referee Szymon Marciniak and UEFA over a host of controversial decisions during their 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League.

The 2022 World Cup final ref pointed to the spot for a soft Sporting penalty in the first half, though Luis Suarez’s spot kick was saved by Senne Lammens. Minutes later Lammens went from hero to zero when rushing out of his goal and taking out Maximiliano Araujo for another penalty. Suarez made amends from 12 yards.

Amad Diallo thought he had equalised, only for his goal to be ruled out for a foul by Youri Tielemans in the build-up, which earned the midfielder a yellow card after some vigorous protests.

Man Utd received a penalty of their own early in the second half also bordered on soft; Lisandro Martinez going down very easily after Eduardo Quaresma’s clumsy challenge.

Bruno Fernandes converted and then two minutes later benefitted from a divot of his own creation, albeit inadvertently, to hand Man Utd the lead, when he low, driven shot flicked up off the pitch to beat keeper Kaique Pereira.

A chaos continued when a Lammens howler saw Sporting equaliser, the keeper failing to deal with a cross to allow Suarez to instinctively, and acrobatically, finish from close range.

And then, at the other end of the pitch, an extremely similar scenario occurred as Pereira palmed the ball into his own net at a Man Utd corner for what appeared to be the winner.

Referee Marciniak initially awarded the goal, but VAR ordered a pitchside review which saw Martinez and Patrick Dorgu penalised for a foul on the keeper. There was still time for a red card as Tielemans was shown a second yellow for a late, studs up challenge.

The performance stirred up plenty of frustrations among the fanbase, especially in light of Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool which was later overturned by the Premier League.

There were plenty of fans, both with an affiliation to Man utd and not, claiming a “robbery”.

A Man Utd fan said one of the decisions “boiled his blood”, while others were left waiting for another apology after the Yoro debacle.

But one Man City fan saw things slightly differently, insisting very decision was “spot on”...

#1719. ‘Disgrace’: Manchester United legend lets rip after Champions League controversy

Ex-Manchester United star Ashley Young labelled the performance of referee Szymon Marciniak during Wednesday’s chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting as a “disgrace”.

Marciniak was at the centre of multiple controversial decisions in a dramatic 2-2 league phase tie in Lisbon, awarding three penalties, ruling out two Man Utd goals and sending off midfielder Youri Tielemans in stoppage time.

New Red Devils boss Mauricio Pochettino claimed that his side had been “punished” by the officials, going on to say that it was “impossible” to understand how the decisions were reached.

‘Apology FC’: Man Utd fans make clear demand after referee ‘robbery’

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal

Man Utd injury update: Amad, Rashford, Baleba latest return dates

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

Young held a similar position, with the former winger left searching for words when speaking about Marciniak’s display.

The ex-United captain said on BBC Radio 5 Live: “The referee’s performance was just simply… wow.

“The decisions that he gave… Youri Tielemans getting booked, to eventually getting sent off later because you booked him when it should never have been a booking, and it should have been an equalising goal.

“The third goal that should have stood because he’s saying Patrick Dorgu fouled the ‘keeper.

“The ‘keeper comes out and flaps at it before he is even touched. How that has gone to VAR is beyond me. His decision-making today is nothing more than a disgrace.”

United fans would have been further irked by the decision to rule out their potential late winner, as Sporting’s equaliser came in a similar fashion. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens dropped a high ball under light pressure, allowing Luis Suarez to convert with an improvised bicycle kick.

However, talkSPORT pundit Gabby Agbonlahor believes the reaction to the refereeing controversies has been overblown.

He said on Thursday morning: “Manchester United fans, just get on with it. You didn’t deserve to win the game.

“Did the referee make a couple of mistakes? Yes, he did. But come on. Manchester United fans - first they’re moaning about the owners, next they’re moaning about chief executives, [Omar] Berrada, [Jason] Wilcox. Now it’s referees every game, it’s VAR every game.

“How about - you didn’t deserve to win the game? The referee didn’t make Lisandro Martinez make a stupid challenge to give away the first penalty that gets saved.

“The referee didn’t make [Noussair] Mazraoui come in so tight to the centre-half and allow the [Sporting] left-back flying forward.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens come out to no man’s land. I don’t know what he’s doing. I don’t know what he’s going to achieve running out there.

“The referee didn’t make Lammens have chocolate wrists and drop the ball when no one is on him.”

The draw with Sporting leaves United 19th in the Champions League table, with three games remaining in this season’s league phase.

Tielemans’ red card means the Belgian will miss their next European fixture - a home tie with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig on December 8.

#1718. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

Wolverhampton: Bentley, Trippier, Mosquera, Toti Gomes, Wolfe, Lopez, Andre Trindade, Munetsi, Rodrigo Gomes, Armstrong, Mane.Subs used: Jiménez 60 (Mateus Mané), ‌Doyle ‌67 (Rodrigo Gomes), ⁠Tchatchoua 67 (Trippier), Pedro Lima 79 (André),Chirewa 79 (Møller Wolfe)Scorers: M. McLoughlin 27, A. Gudjohnsen 48Yellow card: Pickering ​34, Cantwell 35, ‌Forshaw 45Attendance: 30,984Referee: Farai ⁠Hallam

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

Possession: Wolves 52%-48% BlackburnShots: 10-4Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 9-7

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Both teams scored when the other seemed on top slightly.

Wolves have probably shaded it with those efforts from Lopez and Mane which went narrowly over.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. However, Alebiosu, with Mane not far behind him, puts it behind for a corner. Trippier delivers and the Blackburn keeper makes a meal of it, missing his punch out but then scrambles back towards his own goal to gather the loose ball.

The visitors went behind against the run of play but probably deservedly they are back on level terms. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Two goals in the opening half an hour of the new Championship season.

"They STUN Molineux!" 😳Sean Mcloughlin delightfully heads past Dan Bentley to equalise for Blackburn 👏 pic.twitter.com/v5qLhJ0wBt

Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Pickering sends it into a good area and the touch comes off the head of Munetsi, whose header loops into the air and goes just over his own bar for another corner on the other side.

Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

Wolves: Bentley; Trippier, Mosquera, T.Gomes; R.Gomes, André, Munetsi, Möller Wolfe; Lopez, Mané; Armstrong.Substitutes: Sá, Bueno, Jiménez, Lima, Doyle, Chirewa, Djiga, Tchatchoua, Edozie.

Blackburn: Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Forshaw, Montgomery; Afolayan, Cantwell, Morishita; Gudjohnsen.Substitutes: Pears, Ribeiro, Tavares, Morsy, Fevrier, Carter, Henriksson, Ohashi, Garrett.

These do not look good if you are a Blackburn fan; these are their attacking statistics and rankings in the Championship last season:

Goals: 42, 23rdxG performance: -13.9, 24thShots on target: 146, 23rdShot conversion: 7.9%, 22ndChances created: 368, 21st

Near the bottom of the league in every single one of those pretty much.

A debut for our brand new away kit 🤩#WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/Qxyvw1jAgi

Former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes has died aged 79 in the last week and the club he played 382 times for is paying tribute to him tonight:

Paying tribute to a Wolves legend on tonight's matchday programme 🧡 pic.twitter.com/VEHciTuOZq

"We know what we are doing" 🤝Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto is confident in his side ahead of his the first Championship game of the season 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/2m12gsJ2y8

"We're ready for a strong performance" 💪Wolves defender Kieran Trippier and Blackburn's Sam Morsy preview their opening game of the season clash 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/I5t1J9Gapp

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.

The boys are in the Black Country 👋 #WOLvROV | #Rovers 🔵⚪️ pic.twitter.com/WjuGwrxYtQ

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are new playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

“I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our big goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”

They have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray said. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

#1716. Tottenham XI vs Sunderland: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has returned to training ahead of Tottenham’s visit to Sunderland this weekend, but Savio is expected to miss out.

Tonali missed Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last Saturday due to illness, as Roberto De Zerbi’s side earned three points on their return from the international break, but is set to be available for selection when Spurs travel to the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

Savio, meanwhile, was named on the bench against Ipswich, having missed the last four games with a muscular injury. The 22-year-old was introduced in the second half, but lasted just 26 minutes before he had to come off injured.

Savio was visibly upset as he headed down the tunnel, and De Zerbi confirmed he had suffered a recurrence of the same injury that had kept him out for the last six weeks.

"I'm sorry for Savio's injury, because it was the same injury as last time, and we need him. He's a crucial player for us,” De Zerbi said in his post-match press conference.

“He’s unlucky in this period. We have to be close with him to help him to become the top player we bought at the beginning of this season."

Savio is expected to join fellow wingers Mathys Tel and Mykhailo Mudryk on the sidelines, meaning teenage sensation Luca Williams-Barnett, who scored and assisted on his full senior debut against Ipswich, could be in line for more minutes.

Fears over an injury to Omar Marmoush have been allayed after the forward was spotted in training footage.

Centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo is expected to be available for selection again after returning from a calf injury. Tosin was fit to play against Ipswich, but De Zerbi chose not to take any unnecessary risks.

Rodrigo Bentancur could also return to the starting lineup, having been named on the bench against Ipswich after returning late from international duty.

#1715. West Bromwich Albion vs Bristol City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Carter White | 26 Nov 2026 13:09

Looking to gain ground in the race for automatic promotion, West Bromwich Albion welcome Bristol City to The Hawthorns for a Championship contest on Saturday afternoon.

The Baggies are in the midst of an impressive unbeaten run in the second tier, making them the favourites with the best UK betting apps 2026 to record victory over the out-of-form Robins.

Since a 1-0 defeat by Birmingham City at The Hawthorns on October 10, West Brom have strung together an eight-game unbeaten streak (W5 D3) in the Championship, beating Bolton Wanderers last time out.

Wednesday night's match at the Toughsheet Community Stadium provided the stage for Albion's Norwegian stars to shine, with Aune Heggebo (2) and Felix Horn Myhre scoring in a 3-1 success over the Wanderers.

Now boasting the best away record in the division with 17 points collected from nine outings, James Morrison's side are back at The Hawthorns this weekend, when they will be striving for a repeat of their 3-0 battering of Millwall in the Black Country prior to the international break.

One of four Midlands clubs inside the top five of the Championship standings after 17 matches, West Brom are occupying fifth spot in the table, just three points behind pacesetters Middlesbrough and Stoke City.

Scoring an eye-catching eight goals across their past three league fixtures, the Baggies pose danger from an array of positions, with five different players scoring three or more Championship goals so far this term.

Following three consecutive losses at the beginning of their tricky November schedule, Bristol City stopped the rot with a respectable 1-1 draw with Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night.

It looked as if the Robins were hurtling towards their ninth defeat of the league campaign when Joe Worrall opened the scoring early on, however, Cameron Pring's first goal in nearly three years secured a share of the spoils.

Winning just one of his past nine second-tier contests (D3 L5) in charge, Michael Skubala remains under severe pressure at Bristol City, who currently reside in an uninspiring 16th place in the table.

The Robins' sole victory in their current wretched run arrived on the road at Bolton on October 31, when Dom Ballard, Sam Bell and playmaker Scott Twine netted in a five-goal thriller.

Firing an attacking blank in five of their past eight matches ahead of Saturday's trip to The Hawthorns, there is no doubting that the Robins are failing to maximise the potential of Ballard and Lorent Tolaj, with the pair scoring 40 goals combined in League One last term.

After leading goalscorer Isaac Price missed the win at Bolton on Wednesday, West Brom boss Morrison revealed that the Northern Irishman is set to be sidelined for up to six weeks due to a knee injury.

The attacker joins midfielder Ousmane Diakite (calf) in the Albion treatment room, with the Mali international expected to be out until late December.

Right-back Noah Galves (knee) will not play again this season, whilst talented youngster Rabby Nzingoula is suspended for this weekend after collecting his fifth yellow card of the term at Bolton.

There was a serious injury scare for Bristol City on Tuesday night, when centre-back Luke McNally was forced off due to a knee issue.

The 27-year-old has previously missed nearly two years due to a problem with the same knee, meaning that Rob Dickie is likely to be drafted into the XI at The Hawthorns.

Sam Greenwood and Lisav Eissat were surprise omissions from the matchday squad last time out but could return to the fold on Saturday.

West Bromwich Albion possible starting lineup:

O'Leary; Pereira, Mepham, Campbell, Styles; Tunde, Horn Myhre, Molumby, Whitwell; Morgan, Heggebo

Collins; Tanner, Dickie, Atkinson, Pring; Wallace, Knight, Randell, Twine; Tolaj, Ballard

Aiming to extend their unbeaten run to nine matches, West Brom will be confident of beating Bristol City, even with Nzingoula, Price and Diakite all sidelined.

The Robins are certainly capable of producing a gutsy away performance but are likely to suffer defeat in the Black Country this weekend.

#1714. Man City get appeal verdict update ahead of Arsenal clash

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Manchester City have been given an update on their appeal against the Premier League's financial charges ahead of this weekend’s huge title clash with Arsenal.

City were in October found guilty of 114 breaches of the league's financial rules, with an independent commission concluding the club had used "sham" commercial contracts to disguise more than £830million in funding between 2009 and 2018. The commission also found the Man City had made "concerted efforts to stop and frustrate" the investigation.

The club have consistently denied wrongdoing, and an appeal was immediately launched with a result expected in early 2027.

Speculation over possible punishments, should the appeal prove unsuccessful, range from a fine to various points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League, all the while Man City‘s form on the pitch has suffered a dip.

City have won just one of their last five games across all competitions, and have lost three of their last four in the Premier League to see their title hopes handed a huge blow. Arsenal is up next on Sunday in a game Erling Haaland has already described as their “toughest of the season”.

Amid the on-pitch struggles, financial expert Stefan Borson, who previously worked as a financial advisor to City, expects there to be clarity sooner rather than later over the club’s off-pitch concerns.

"We're told that it will be mid-December,” Borson said, regarding the appeal hearing, on Football Uncensored with Piers Morgan and Simon Jordan.

“Because of the way the days fall, that's likely to start on the 12th.

"It's likely to go for between five and 10 days, it seems, and therefore finish before Christmas. And then we wait for a decision. Ordinarily, that decision would take quite some time.

"I suspect that certainly the Premier League want to get it expedited so they get a decision and can then have the sanction hearing and the sanction appeal, which is inevitable either way, in before the end of the season so they can effectively sanction City and punish them this season."

Borson suggested a timetable may already have been agreed, with the Premier League keen to avoid further legal complications.

"In the rulebook that came out at the start of the season, the rules changed and you had an expedited timetable. In any event, a case like City's and an appeal like City's would never fall within the standardised timetable.

"I think most likely the parties have ultimately agreed some form of timetable which means that any argument from City in the future about the process goes away.

"The last thing the Premier League will want is to give City another reason to take legal action under Rule X or otherwise and to say, actually the whole appeal process, not only was the old process flawed but we didn't even have a fair appeal. Because if they do that, we're back to square one."

#1713. Martin Odegaard critics are wrong - Arsenal must give him what he deserves

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

A quick glance at two contrasting stats sums up exactly where Arsenal’s shortcomings lie at the moment.

Mikel Arteta’s side are still in fine shape to progress straight through to the last 16 as one of the top-eight sides in the Champions League. Only the Gunners, holders Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid remain unbeaten in this season’s competition.

However, it could have been so much better, after an extraordinarily wasteful display in the draw with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night. Arsenal registered 30 shots, but only four on target and they scored just once.

It should have been so much more for Martin Odegaard, too. He has registered only one assist in Europe this season, ranking him 45th in the competition for that metric.

And yet for expected assists, per FotMob, Odegaard ranks top across the entire Champions League. Above Nico Paz, who has five assists to his name, and Lamine Yamal, who has three.

Arsenal have had no issue creating chances. Against Dortmund, Odegaard laid on nine of them, the most by any player in a Champions League match this season.

That was just the second time this decade that an Arsenal player has created more than five chances in a Champions League match. The other example? Odegaard against Napoli in September.

The discourse around Odegaard is often hypercritical. That, to an extent, is understandable. He has been the captain and creative heartbeat of the team in a period in which, for all it has been successful, there have been ongoing questions surrounding the attack.

It is perhaps also a hangover from the last two seasons, when injuries hampered Odegaard and he was well off his best. Frustration towards him built and some minds appear to have been made up.

However, the criticism that he does not deliver consistently enough just does not hold up to scrutiny this season.

Man City get appeal verdict update ahead of Arsenal clash

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal

Tottenham beat Arsenal to exciting transfer coup as signing confirmed

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

From the moment Odegaard returned to the club in the summer after a strong World Cup with Norway, he has looked back to his best. That started with his sublime goal against Manchester City in the Community Shield and has continued since.

For all there have been some notable exceptions, Arsenal have on the whole played much better football this season. They have been far more free-flowing and fluid in attack.

Odegaard has been central to that. Along with his chance creation stats in Europe, Odegaard is also second for expected assists in the Premier League.

He is taking more responsibility in front of goal, too. Odegaard is Arsenal’s top scorer this season and is only one league goal shy of his combined tally from the last two seasons.

If there has been a dip in Arsenal’s attack from the start of this season, that is not down to Odegaard. Bukayo Saka, who was displaying far better goalscoring instincts, suffering a quad injury, and Kai Havertz’s performance levels dropping significantly are far more relevant explanations.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard

Odegaard has been the most consistent forward player. It is not just the chances created or even the goals, but his influence in all facets of Arsenal’s game as almost an extension of Arteta on the pitch. He is the leader of the press, and that led to the winning goal against Liverpool at Anfield earlier this month.

Arsenal do have a problem in attack - but it is not Odegaard. It is not an exaggeration to say that Viktor Gyokeres should have scored another three goals against Dortmund from chances created by Odegaard alone.

The Gunners are not clinical enough but that is not the fault of the player creating the chances. Nor is it a coaching issue. Arteta could not have done more to deliver a win against Dortmund.

The problem is a personnel one. The quality of Arsenal’s attackers does not come close to matching the level in every other position in the squad. At least one top-class winger signing is required, along with a new striker.

It was clear at the end of last season that significant upgrades were needed. Instead, Arsenal sold three forwards and signed only Christos Tzolis.

That is the big failure and where the fingers should be pointing. Not at Odegaard for occasionally taking too many touches or making a wrong decision on the counter.

Odegaard’s contract situation adds another factor to the debate over his role in the team. He is nearing the final 18 months of his current deal.

Talks have not yet begun over an extension, Odegaard revealed during the international break, but that should be a no-brainer for Arsenal.

That will require the club to make another significant financial commitment, following on from several other new contracts for key players, but it is still a far cheaper alternative to trying to sign a replacement of Odegaard’s quality.

Securing Odegaard’s future should be the club’s next top priority, swiftly followed by then delivering him the forwards he deserves.

#1712. Wirtz feeling confident heading into crucial Merseyside Derby

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Florian Wirtz insisted confidence is coursing through Liverpool's veins ahead of this Sunday's Merseyside derby following a superb midweek in the Champions League.

Liverpool boosted their hopes of a top-eight finish in the competition with a 3-0 win over Club Brugge, with Wirtz's 79th-minute strike coming either side of Alexander Isak's brace.

The Reds have now won their last three matches in all competitions, with their last Premier League encounter seeing them thrash rivals Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield.

And Wirtz has been key to that run of form. After a fruitful international break with Germany and former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp, he has now scored in three consecutive appearances for the first time since moving to Merseyside last summer.

Indeed, it's the first time he has achieved the feat overall at club level since September 2024 for Bayer Leverkusen, while Isak will fancy his chances of scoring away from home.

Among all Premier League players, Isak has scored the joint-most away goals across all competitions this season (eight – level with Erling Haaland). His total is already more than any Liverpool player managed away from home in the 2025-26 campaign (six by Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Virgil van Dijk).

"We have so many good players in our team and I think even when we can substitute some wingers or strikers in the 60th minute or later, I think that gives us a lot," Wirtz said of Liverpool's attack ahead of making the short trip to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

"I think it shows how good our team is, and I think it's important for a top team to also have a strong bench to bring on good players.

"I think the last two games were really good, and it's always good to go into such a game with two games like this. We're really happy about this and confidence is there for sure."

Everton, meanwhile, come into Sunday's fixture off the back of a 4-0 defeat away to Brentford in what was David Moyes' 593rd game in charge of the Toffees.

Keane Lewis-Potter scored twice in two minutes before captain James Tarkowski was sent off for the first time in the Premier League five minutes before the break.

A stunner from Vitaly Janelt and a goal from substitute Fabio Carvalho compounded Moyes to his biggest Premier League defeat while in charge of Everton since losing 1-6 at home to Arsenal on the opening matchday of the 2009-10 season.

But with rivals Liverpool up next, Everton defender Jake O'Brien believes the Merseyside derby provides the Toffees with the ideal motivation to bounce back.

"It was really bad from start to finish," O'Brien said after the Brentford defeat. "It was a knock-on effect of decisions and mistakes, and it carried on from there, really.

"There's no excuses. We were really bad, but I think we can put this behind us.

"We’re much better than this and we know we’ve got big games coming up, especially [against Liverpool]. It was a really bad game and we apologise to all the fans who travelled.

"But I think we can put this behind us, and there’s no better game to come in firing and change things around."

Despite failing to get on the scoresheet against Brentford, Barry still proved to be a handful in the final third, and Everton will need their top scorer at his very best.

Barry has scored (five) or assisted (one) six of the Toffees' last seven league goals, though he has failed to net in his two previous Premier League games against Liverpool.

Wirtz has scored and assisted a goal in his last two Premier League appearances, and after a positive display in the Champions League, he will look to do the same here.

The only Liverpool player to do so three times in a row is Mohamed Salah, who did it twice in December 2018 and October 2021.

Flo Eight goal contributions in his last five games for club and country https://t.co/UvRELxk34P

Liverpool have lost just one of their last 15 Premier League away games against Everton (W4 D10), with 10 of their last 14 visits finishing level.

The Reds have scored six 90th-minute winning goals against Everton in the Premier League, more than any side has against another. This exact fixture last season was settled by Virgil van Dijk's stoppage-time winner.

Iraola's side have also won each of their last four Premier League away games. They last had a longer run between May and September 2021 (five) and last did so within the same season between November 2019 and February 2020 (eight).

Everton, meanwhile, have won two of their last three Premier League games, though they lost 4-0 to Brentford last time out. It's as many victories as they'd managed in their previous 15 (D7 L6).

The Toffees have won just two of their last 31 Premier League games against Liverpool (D14 L15), beating them 2-0 at Anfield in February 2021 and 2-0 at Goodison Park in April 2024.

And you can expect a feisty encounter here. Everton vs Liverpool has had more red cards than any other fixture in Premier League history (25), while the Toffees hold the record for most red cards overall in the competition (114).

#1711. Flares turn Stamford Bridge red as ‘30,000 Fenerbahce fans’ take over Chelsea’s home

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Stamford Bridge was lit up last night by Fenerbahce fans' flares as Chelsea's home ground continued to host Shakhtar Donetsk's Champions League games.

The Ukrainian giants are this season playing their home European games in west London due to Russia's ongoing invasion of their home country, having in previous seasons staged their home games in Poland, Germany and Slovenia.

The matches have attracted local and travelling Ukrainian football fans, along with thousands of rivals supporters as Greek side AEK Athens and Portuguese outfit Sporting came to town earlier this season. Real Madrid will visit at the end of January.

Wednesday night saw Fenerbahce as the visiting team, and the fanbase came in numbers.

Stamford Bridge was glowing red from the light of flares ahead of the game, while footage of supporters descending on west London and the surrounding Chelsea area spread across social media.

As the designated away team, Fenerbahce were allocated the 'Shed End' of Stamford Bridge, which is said to hold around 6,000 fans, but thousands more were seen across 'home' sections of the stadium.

The tickets went on general sale earlier in November, which allows any member of the "general public" to purchase.

Fenerbahce won the game 1-0 and, speaking after the game, Ismail Yüksek said: “There were nearly 30,000 Fenerbahce fans in the stadium today

"You wouldn’t see anything like this at any other club in the world. They gave us incredible support. They were amazing. They gave us incredible strength. I dedicate this victory to them.

"From the first minute to the last, the team fought just as hard as our fans. We deserved this victory from start to finish."

#1710. Omar Marmoush injury update as new Tottenham footage emerges

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Fears that Omar Marmoush has picked up an injury have been allayed after the Tottenham forward was pictured in training ahead of Sunday’s trip to Sunderland.

Concerns had grown online this week that Marmoush was set for a period on the sidelines, with speculation he was set to visit a knee specialist.

The 27-year-old came off the bench during Spurs’ 2-0 victory at home to Ipswich last weekend and did not appear to pick up an injury, as Roberto De Zerbi’s side returned to winning ways at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Inevitably, though, concerns had gained traction and Marmoush’s involvement against Sunderland had been considered doubtful.

Spurs have dismissed the claims as online speculation, and footage of Marmoush on the Hotspur Way training pitches was posted on the club’s social media on Thursday.

In a major boost for De Zerbi, who is currently sweating over the fitness of several attacking players, the Egyptian international now appears fit and available for selection.

Spurs are expected to be without wingers Mykhailo Mudryk, Mathys Tel and Savio against Sunderland, so Marmoush being able to deputise on the flanks as well as through the middle will give De Zerbi more options heading into the weekend.

Mudryk is still struggling with an ankle ligament injury, with De Zerbi suggesting last week the Chelsea loanee had suffered a setback in his recovery.

Tel, meanwhile, is expected to be out for up to three weeks after sustaining an ankle injury against Leeds before the international week.

With Mudryk and Tel absent against Ipswich, De Zerbi selected Savio in a matchday squad for the first time since October 10 after he suffered a muscular injury in training.

The Brazilian was introduced from the bench in the 64th minute, but had to come off again after suffering a recurrence of the muscular injury that had kept him out for the last six weeks.

#1709. Le Havre vs. Strasbourg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 26 Nov 2026 13:09

Two of Ligue 1's struggling sides meet in Saturday's gameweek 12 encounter, as winless Le Havre host third-bottom Strasbourg at Stade Oceane.

The bottom club remain the only side without a victory in the French top flight after 11 matches, leaving their survival prospects looking increasingly bleak even at this stage of the campaign.

Le Havre's 14th-placed finish last season, just three points above Nice in the relegation playoff spot, offered little encouragement ahead of the 2026-27 campaign, and those concerns have proved justified.

Le Club Doyen have not won a top-flight fixture since beating Lorient 2-0 on the final day of last season, with their miserable start prompting Didier Digard's dismissal at the end of October.

Valerien Ismael's first match in charge of the basement club began brightly when Josh Maja scored after three minutes against Troyes; however, they held that advantage for just 15 minutes before eventually losing 3-1.

Conceding three more goals left Les Ciel et Marine with the competition's joint-worst defensive record, having shipped 25, while their tally of 10 scored surpasses only Angers' nine.

Even victory would do little to transform the Dean Club's position, as they enter this weekend eight points behind the relegation playoff spot and nine adrift of safety.

Nonetheless, the hosts must avoid defeat to Vitor Matos's Strasbourg, who occupy that playoff position.

Le Racing's disappointing start has already cost Hugo Oliveira his job, with Matos replacing his Portuguese compatriot during the international break.

The new manager's debut did not go to plan, with Le RCS losing 1-0 to Brest despite an encouraging performance in which they attempted 15 shots to their opponents' 16; Le Racing also created two chances deemed clear-cut to Brest's one.

Looking to build on that display, Le RCS target their fourth victory of the campaign this weekend, although it would be only their second since early October.

Maximum points could lift Matos's men out of the playoff spot and as high as 13th, although escaping the bottom three also requires Auxerre, Troyes or Le Mans to slip up.

The hosts have several absentees, with Felix Mambimbi (Achilles), Timothee Pembele (muscle), Rassoul Ndiaye (muscle), Daren Mosengo (ankle), Stephan Zagadou (ACL), Sota Nakamura (leg) and Lionel Mpasi (Achilles) all sidelined.

Enzo Koffi begins a two-match suspension following his late dismissal against Troyes last weekend, ruling him out of Saturday's encounter and December's trip to Lens.

Only six players have surpassed Maja's five league goals this season, but the Nigerian's efforts have brought little reward for a Dean Club side repeatedly undermined by defensive frailties.

Strasbourg have several potential game-changers, with Gessime Yassine registering four goals and three assists, Giovanni Reyna scoring three, Conrad Harder and Dario Essugo contributing two goals and an assist and Sebastian Nanasi setting up three.

However, Reyna is unavailable due to a muscle problem, while Fabio Balde (leg), Oso (knock) and Joaquin Panichelli (ACL) are also sidelined.

Bodart; Sasso, Seko, Touba; Ouziad, Mwanga, Ebonog, Richardson, Jelert; Maja, Fofana

Jorgensen; Antwi, Doukoure, Coulibaly, Hogsberg; Essugo, El Mourabet; Yassine, Nanasi, Godo; Harder

Maja's scoring form offers Le Havre some encouragement, but conceding 25 goals in 11 matches suggests that their defensive problems remain too pronounced for an immediate recovery.

Strasbourg created enough chances to trouble Brest in Matos's first match and should find greater reward against the division's joint-leakiest defence.

#1708. Manchester United XI vs Brentford: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Mauricio Pochettino’s first home game as Manchester United boss sees them welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday, with the hosts desperate for three points.

Pochettino is still figuring out how best to set up his new team, first opting for a back three in the 4-0 drubbing by Liverpool at Anfield last weekend before then switching to a four-man defence for the chaotic Champions League draw with Sporting on Wednesday.

Although Brentford will fancy their chances of victory based on the respective league positions of the two clubs - Man Utd 19th, the Bees in sixth - United will be urged by their fans to attack. As such, a more timid back three seems unlikely.

It will be a case of balancing fitness levels with only two days of rest between games. Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has come under fire in recent weeks for his performances, but back-up Karl Darlow has struggled with injury since arriving in the summer.

Pochettino’s defensive options are fairly limited. Leny Yoro is available after his early red card against Liverpool was overturned, while Harry Maguire was restored to the starting XI for the Sporting game.

Brentford’s pace in behind may necessitate a quicker backline, meaning Maguire could be dropped once again here.

Lisandro Martinez has been at left-back, but Patrick Dorgu’s attacking qualities will likely be required on Saturday and Luke Shaw is also now back in training. By moving Martinez back to centre-half alongside Yoro, Pochettino can find the pace required.

Diogo Dalot may get the nod ahead of Noussair Mazraoui at right-back.

Pochettino has quickly settled on a midfield partnership of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans, who was controversially sent off late on against Sporting but is available in the Premier League.

The attackers in front of them almost pick themselves - Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and captain Bruno Fernandes will all be involved in some capacity. However, their exact positions are subject to change.

Fernandes was deployed on the left behind Cunha in the defeat by Liverpool, while Mbeumo was briefly used as the lone forward under Michael Carrick.

#1707. Moretto claims Camarda’s ‘real exit door’ is abroad rather than in Italy: “Trying a different experience”

There’s been a lot said about Francesco Camarda’s future in recent months and it seems AC Milan are getting closer to a decision.

Put simply, Milan are in the same situation that they were a few years ago. Camarda isn’t playing and when he does, he’s not really getting the most out of games. So, another loan will be sought in the mercato.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His time with Lecce previously wasn’t exactly fruitful, but he did grab a first Serie A goal, which helped. However, he’s still without a competitive goal for the Rossoneri and his minutes aren’t regular. In other words, it’s looking like another six months wasted.

So, he’ll leave the nest in January once again.

Talk of a move abroad has been really common recently, and it seems increasingly likely that his next test will be abroad. However, there are no inklings about where it may be, even in Matteo Moretto’s latest update on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, as MilanNews relays.

“AC Milan ‘s decision has essentially already been made: they want the boy to be able to play consistently and consistently, trying a different experience.

“There’s been a lot of talk about Cagliari, there’s been a lot of talk about Genoa, there’s been a lot of talk about Italy, but as I’ve said in recent days, keep an eye on options that lead abroad.

“It’s true that there are Italian teams interested in Camarda, but as of today, I can’t see Genoa and Cagliari pursuing the player, despite preliminary discussions. Cagliari, in particular, had inquired about the terms, but nothing more and nothing less.

“This solution, from what I understand, is unlikely to go ahead. I might keep a small door open to Italy for you, but the real door is a door that leads abroad.

“Keep an eye on foreign championships, keep an eye on championships and teams that give confidence to young people, that let young people play and that give young people space. So, as of today, this is the line on Camarda.”

#1706. Liverpool XI vs Everton: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Liverpool are full of confidence as they travel to face rivals Everton in the latest Merseyside derby on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola’s surging Reds have been piling up the goals since the November international break - scoring seven times across their last two fixtures alone.

A hugely satisfying 4-0 dismantling of Manchester United at Anfield last weekend in what was Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge of the visitors was quickly followed by a 3-0 victory in the Champions League away at Club Brugge.

Their two statement signings from last summer - Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak - are both hitting top form, which bodes well for this weekend’s derby showdown.

Iraola will likely already know his starting XI for the short trip to Everton, based on the strong form of his team.

Stalwart Alisson will start in goal, while Virgil van Dijk will return to captain the side after being rested in Belgium on Wednesday night.

Ronald Araujo will be shifted to right-back as it is unlikely that Jeremie Frimpong will be asked to play twice in the span of five days following injury.

Jeremy Jacquet will partner Van Dijk in central defence, while Milos Kerkez looks set to make his 90th appearance under Iraola - the left-back having been trusted by his head coach at both Liverpool and Bournemouth.

Dominik Szoboszlai seems to have put his injury woes in the past, and while young Trey Nyoni has impressed when given opportunities this term, Alexis Mac Allister will surely get the nod alongside him in the midfield engine room as Ryan Gravenberch remains a doubt.

The aforementioned Wirtz is playing the best football of his Liverpool career to date; Rio Ngumoha and Bradley Barcola look set to line up either side of the German, with Victor Munoz forced off injured against Brugge to join Cody Gakpo in the treatment room.

#1705. Man City XI vs Arsenal: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, injury latest for Premier League

Manchester City head to Arsenal this weekend in desperate need of a morale-boosting victory.

Enzo Maresca’s side have picked up just one point from the last 12 available in the Premier League, with a disappointing home draw with Fulham following successive defeats at the hands of Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest.

Sitting third and already six points behind leaders Arsenal after 11 games, many pundits predict that City’s title chances will effectively be over if they lose in north London on Sunday.

City are also still waiting for their appeal to be heard against the guilty verdict returned by an independent panel back in September on their charges of breaching the Premier League’s financial rules across a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2017/18. They deny any wrongdoing.

Head coach Enzo Maresca has to find the right team to beat an Arsenal side that have lost just twice at home in 2026.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will start in goal as usual, with the back four in front of him likely consisting of Matheus Nunes, Ruben Dias, Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol.

Dias was rested for the home draw with Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday, with the City captain set to be restored to the starting XI here.

Nico O’Reilly has emerged as the first-choice option at left-back in recent weeks, but the defensive ability of Gvardiol could be key in a cagey match.

Maresca has experimented with the construction of his midfield in the last few matches. Enzo Fernandez was deployed as a No10 against Napoli, but a return to the preferred paring of the Argentine and Elliot Anderson at the base of City’s midfield feels likely at Arsenal.

Similarly, Iliman Ndiaye has impressed on the right wing in recent weeks. Rayan Cherki was deployed out wide against Napoli, but has been most effective as a No10.

Jeremy Doku has become trusted on the left, while Erling Haaland cannot be left out - even if he is enduring a goalscoring drought by his usual lofty standards.

#1704. The Numbers Game: Brazil and Argentina go head-to-head as Palmeiras clash with Estudiantes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Once again, the Copa Libertadores final features teams from South America's two powerhouse nations.

Brazil and Argentina will be represented at Estadio Centenario in Montevideo by Palmeiras and Estudiantes, respectively.

Brazil and Argentina are level with 25 titles each in Libertadores history. Having won each of the last seven editions, teams from Brazil hold the longest all-time run of consecutive titles, but they have never led the outright charts for most trophies lifted in the competition, having last equalled the record with Uruguay in 1963 (two titles each).

Palmeiras are playing in their eighth Libertadores final, a tally reached only by Boca Juniors (12) and Penarol (10). They are looking for their fourth title, which would see them equal Flamengo as Brazil's most successful club in the competition.

Estudiantes, on the other hand, are playing in their sixth final in search of their fifth title, a number of trophies only Independiente (seven), Boca (six) and Penarol (five) have achieved so far.

Estudiantes have reached five Libertadores finals, winning four of them (80% success rate). This is the second-highest rate among teams that have played at least three finals, level with Flamengo and surpassed only by Independiente (100%, 7/7).

However, they last reached a final in 2009, when they beat another Brazilian team, Cruzeiro.

Here, using Opta data, we look at the key storylines ahead of the clash at Estadio Centenario.

¡PALMEIRAS VS. ESTUDIANTES, la gran Final de la CONMEBOL #Libertadores!  Jugarán en Montevideo por la #GloriaEterna https://t.co/b1PMjY9DuA

— CONMEBOL Libertadores (@Libertadores) October 23, 2026

This is the second Libertadores season in which Palmeiras and Estudiantes will face off.

The first time was also a final, which took place at the Estadio Centenario, in 1968.

Estudiantes won a tie-breaker 2-0, after a 3-1 win for Palmeiras in the first leg and a 2-1 victory for the Argentine team in the second.

Estudiantes have opened the scoring in 12 CONMEBOL tournament matches against Brazilian sides since the 2017 season, winning 11 of those (D1). Furthermore, they have conceded just two goals in those encounters.

Through their first seven games in the 2026 Libertadores, Palmeiras used mostly four-at-the-back in-possession shapes (4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 4-2-4), compared to a back-three over their last five (3-4-3, 3-4-1-2, 3-2-4-1).

Just 11% of Palmeiras' passes in the 2026 Libertadores have been long, which is their lowest percentage in a single edition of the competition since Opta began recording this data in 2013.

So Palmeiras are probably going to try and play it out patiently, but could that suit Estudiantes?

Estudiantes have forced the most shot-ending high turnovers (final 40m of the pitch) in the 2026 Libertadores, both overall (23) and on a per-game basis (1.9).

Opta's supercomputer has run 10,000 data-led simulations, and Palmeiras are the favourites.

The Brazilian giants came out victorious in 54.1% of the model's simulations, while Estudiantes were crowned champions 23.4% of the time.

Palmeiras are the joint-leading scorers in the Libertadores this season (17 goals), level with Flamengo, while they have accumulated a tournament-leading 21.1 xG.

But Palmeiras have kept only three clean sheets, conceding 11 goals from 8.5 xGA.

Estudiantes have not been free-scoring, netting 12 in as many matches, but they have kept it tighter than Palmeiras at the other end, recording five shutouts and shipping only seven goals, though they have actually given up chances worth a combined 9.7 xGA.

Palmeiras boast Libertadores final experience

Palmeiras last won this title in 2021, while they competed in last year's final, losing to Flamengo.

Their coach, Abel Ferreira, is taking charge of his fourth Libertadores final. Only Carlos Bianchi (five) has managed more such matches, with Ferreira now drawing level with Luis Cubilla, Roberto Scarone and Luiz Felipe Scolari.

Should he lead Palmeiras to victory, Ferreira will become the joint-second-most successful coach in Libertadores history, matching Osvaldo Zubeldia, who won three titles with, coincidentally, Estudiantes. Bianchi (three titles with Boca Juniors and one with Velez Sarsfield) has won the Libertadores the most times as a coach.

#Aeroporco #PelaGlóriaEtern4 https://t.co/85FKHCD2xm

— SE Palmeiras (@Palmeiras) November 26, 2026

And Ferreira is not the only person in the Palmeiras ranks to boast plenty of Libertadores experience.

Gustavo Gomez will play in his fourth Libertadores final, all of which have come while at Palmeiras (2020, 2021, 2025 and 2026). He will be only the second Paraguayan to feature in that many finals, after Jorge Guasch (1979, 1989, 1990 and 1991 with Olimpia).

Lining up behind defender Gomez is set to be Carlos Miguel, who has saved six of the 21 penalties he has faced for Palmeiras (14 goals conceded, one off target).

Five of these saves came in penalty shoot-outs (three in the 2026 Libertadores) and one in normal time, in the 2026 Paulista final.

Miguel's counterpart, Fernando Muslera, is enjoying the longest run of Libertadores clean sheets in his career, with three between the semi-finals against Flamengo and the quarter-final second leg against Corinthians.

The former Uruguay stalwart could become only the second goalkeeper to win the title without conceding in both the semi-finals and the final, after Agustin Rossi for Flamengo in 2025.

At the other end, Estudiantes are reliant on Guido Carrillo, who is the club's all-time leading scorer in the Libertadores with 14 goals, ahead of Juan Ramon Veron and Mauro Boselli (13 each).

Both Veron and Boselli scored in finals won by the Pincha: Veron netted three goals against Palmeiras in 1968, and Boselli scored one against Cruzeiro in 2009.

Carrillo is Estudiantes' joint-top scorer in this season's tournament, level with Tiago Palacios on three goals. Jose Manuel 'Flaco' Lopez is Palmeiras' leading scorer (four goals in 12 games).

Lopez leads the tournament in successful take-ons (26), while Carrillo leads in aerial duels won (57).

El color de Libertadores Experience  https://t.co/DWWne2gBl1

— Estudiantes de La Plata (@EdelpOficial) November 26, 2026

Marlon Freitas played a crucial role in Palmeiras' semi-final first-leg victory over Fluminense – a 2-1 win at the Maracana.

Along with scoring what proved to be the winner, Freitas led his team-mates for chances created (two), touches (68), accurate passes (48), possession wins (six) and tackles won (3/4), while also winning four of his six duels.

Centre-back Leandro Gonzalez Pirez helped Estudiantes keep clean sheets across both semi-final legs against Flamengo.

In the second leg, he recorded a team-high six clearances, while also recording the joint-most interceptions (three), winning 100% of his aerial duels (2/2) and even creating a chance at the other end.
