#1703. Chelsea: Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo injury latest as Xabi Alonso issues three-man update

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Joao Pedro remains sidelined but Moises Caicedo is available as Chelsea prepare for Friday night’s trip to to Nottingham Forest.

The Brazilian has not played since last month’s 2-0 win at Everton due to a thigh injury, and his absence has seen Chelsea’s form take a hit.

Joao Pedro began this season in fine form, scoring five times and assisting a further three goals in the Blues’ opening six games of the campaign before injury struck.

Caicedo has endured an injury-hit start to the campaign, and was last week forced off during the first half of the 4-1 home defeat to Leeds. Alonso confirmed at the time that the midfielder was “in pain” and would need to be assessed before the trip to the City Ground.

Asked if Joao Pedro, who visited former club Watford on Wednesday night, was fit, Alonso simply replied: “No.”

On Caicedo, he said: “He is going to be okay for tomorrow.”

Alonso was more coy when pushed for an update on Maxence Lacroix, who it was reported this week could be return from injury before the end of the year.

#1702. Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

Newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

Corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

Good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

The game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

On the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the new season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

New manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#1701. Not a forward: Why Mikel Arteta may need to bolster surprise Arsenal position amid January twist

By Lewis Blain | 26 Nov 2026 13:11

Arsenal could face an unexpected transfer decision in January, with Kepa Arrizabalaga's future at the Emirates Stadium uncertain.

The Spanish goalkeeper is understood to be unhappy with his current situation and is not ruling out a mid-season departure.

A potential exit would leave Gunners boss Mikel Arteta needing to consider an additional goalkeeper, despite other areas of his squad appearing to require greater attention.

Kepa joined Arsenal from Chelsea in July 2025 and spent the past 18 months as David Raya's deputy, making 12 appearances in all competitions, including just one in the Premier League.

He has started only twice this season, with his latest appearance coming in Tuesday's 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League, when Raya was unavailable through injury.

Reports in Spain (via Sport Witness) have linked the 32-year-old with Valencia, with sporting director Braulio Vazquez reportedly exploring the possibility of bringing him back to LaLiga.

It is understood that there is nothing concrete at this stage, with Kepa yet to receive a formal approach or offer from the Spanish club.

The shot-stopper has also not held talks with Arsenal over his future, although the possibility of him initiating discussions with the club's hierarchy has not been ruled out.

Kepa's contract at the Emirates runs until 2028, but his future remains uncertain, with Valencia potentially revisiting their interest in the January window.

Arsenal have obvious priorities elsewhere, particularly in attack, where additional options on the wing and at centre-forward could strengthen Arteta's squad as they look to defend their Premier League crown.

However, allowing Kepa to leave in January, even on loan, would create an unexpected problem between the posts.

With Raya, Kepa and Illan Meslier currently providing the goalkeeping options, losing the Spaniard would leave the Gunners needing to consider another addition to maintain sufficient cover.

The club would surely prefer to avoid that situation until the summer, and that makes sense given the other areas that could demand investment.

Unless Kepa pushes for an exit or Valencia make an offer that Arsenal are willing to consider, keeping him until the end of the season would appear the simplest solution.

#1700. Chelsea XI vs Nottingham Forest: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso still has injury issues to solve as Chelsea look to put damaging defeats behind them on Friday night at Nottingham Forest.

Back-to-back losses to Sunderland and Leeds has put pressure on Alonso and his players as they head to struggling Forest.

In a welcome injury update, key midfielder Moises Caicedo has been declared fit to play less than a week after being forced off during the first half against Leeds.

But Alonso also confirmed that neither Joao Pedro nor Maxence Lacroix will be available.

Joao Pedro has been sidelined for a number of weeks with a thigh injury, during which time Chelsea’s form has taken a significant dip.

Young striker Emmanuel Emegha has deputised in the Brazilian’s absence, and he will hope his first goal for the club, coming last week against Leeds, will be enough to see him retain his place this weekend.

A decision must be made over whether to stick with the 4-2-3-1 system or revert to the 3-4-2-1 formation Chelsea were deploying earlier in the season.

It remains unclear when Joao Pedro, Jorrel Hato or Lacroix will return, amid suggestions that the latter could be back before the start of 2027.

#1699. Chelsea: Xabi Alonso breaks silence on Wesley Fofana interview controversy - ‘It won’t be repeated’

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for an interview not authorised by the club that caused controversy this week.

The French centre-back was strongly criticised by fans following comments made about missing a crucial penalty during Chelsea’s Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by Liverpool last month.

Fofana spoke for two-and-a-half hours with YouTuber Zack Nani, who has since insisted on social media that “several quotes were taken out of context or plainly made up in England”.

Asked about the situation at a press conference held before Friday night’s trip to Nottingham Forest in the Premier League, Chelsea head coach Xabi Alonso said: “We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. He has apologised.

“It was not right, he has said it is not going to be repeated, these types of things.”

Fofana missed the decisive penalty that saw Chelsea’s Carabao Cup run end in the fourth round with a 6-5 shootout loss at Anfield following a 1-1 draw, blazing his spot-kick over the crossbar after Emmanuel Emegha had seen an effort saved by Giorgi Mamardashvili and Valentin Barco hit the woodwork.

He had also given away a penalty in normal time for handball that was converted by Cody Gakpo just three minutes after Morgan Rogers had given Chelsea the lead from 12 yards, continuing what has been a difficult season for him so far.

“The Liverpool match was tough to take, but I moved on quickly because that’s just part of football,” Fofana was quoted as saying during the interview with Nani.

“I took responsibility for the penalty - I missed it - and, well, I knew I wasn’t a good penalty taker to begin with, you know [laughs]?”

He continued: “So, I just thought, ‘Okay, I’ll own it.’ But I ended up conceding a penalty during the match - it was a handball - but that’s just part of the game. I could have avoided it; it’s the kind of thing we talk about - you have to be consistent, and you have to keep improving in those areas.

“But after the penalty, I stepped up, because I’m one of the most experienced players. Out on the field, there were a lot of young guys. And, well, you had to get out there, you know?

“You’ve got to go for it. And the way I look at it, if I fail, well, I’ve been through things. I’ve lived through a lot. If I fail, it’s not that it’s not a big deal - sure, it sucks, obviously - but as for me, if I’m the one being attacked, it’s no big deal.

Chelsea XI vs Nottm Forest: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal

“It’s not the first time I’ve been attacked. It’s fine; it doesn’t matter. I couldn’t care less. I know there’s another match in three days.

“In three days’ time, you win, and people forget. They’ve already forgotten about your penalty. That’s just how football works. I stepped up, took it, and missed.

“I sent a real beauty of a shot way over the bar. Did you see my shot? I really blasted it high [laughs]. I remember a fan, way up high, he actually managed to catch the ball. But yeah, I missed, you know.

“Now, I laugh about it because it’s just part of football - that’s how it goes. And, well, there you have it.

“Besides, as I said, we kept the momentum going, we got the win [against Manchester United three days later], and it sort of faded into the background. We actually saw a great response in the second half.”

Fofana also revealed in the interview that he had considered retirement under previous boss Enzo Maresca, having suffered with repeated injury issues since joining Chelsea from Leicester for £70million in the summer of 2022.

#1698. Opposition insight for Olympiacos-Milan: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to start a Europa League comeback, if you will, in Greece tomorrow against an Olympiacos side who are flying.

From their last trip to Olympiacos, Milan know that getting three points tomorrow night will not be easy. Unfortunately, it comes at a time when they really do need easy points.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In terms of qualifying for the knockout phase, their best hopes are currently finishing in the top 24 and getting through the Round of 16 knockout tie. However, a win on Thursday could open hopes of a top eight finish…

➤ Manager: Imanol Alguacil Barrenetxea ➤ Form (all comps): W-W-D-D-W (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Europa League): Hezze, Yaremchuk, Gonzalez – 1 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Freuler, Chiquinho – 1 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

Olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

The spending was almost totally offset by four big sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

In the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey is the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical issues, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

#1697. Arsenal XI vs Man City: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup, Raya injury latest for Premier League

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal are set to make a late decision on the fitness of David Raya ahead of Manchester City’s trip to north London on Sunday.

The Spaniard missed the draw with Borussia Dortmund due to the shoulder injury he picked up at St James’ Park last weekend.

However, while there were fears that was a significant problem, scans have showed that Raya avoided serious injury and his time on the sidelines is not expected to be a lengthy one.

It remains to be seen whether Raya recovers in time to face City on Sunday, with Kepa Arrizabalaga ready to fill in again if required.

Ezri Konsa appears set to keep his place at centre-back, as Arsenal continue to cautiously manage William Saliba’s fitness.

Saliba was in the matchday squad against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund but is yet to make a first-team appearance this season. It would be a surprise if he came straight back in to face City.

It is expected that Riccardo Calafiori will return to the starting line-up after being rested in midweek, while Eberechi Eze could well get the nod in front of him on the left wing after impressing at St James’ Park.

Viktor Gyokeres scored against Dortmund but Kai Havertz is usually trusted in these games by Mikel Arteta.

The German was given a full rest in that draw with Dortmund and he looks set to lead the line against City.

Arteta will provide an update on the latest Arsenal team news at his press conference on Friday afternoon.

#1696. Xabi Alonso reveals details of Chelsea talks after Leeds thrashing

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Xabi Alonso has revealed what he discussed with Chelsea’s hierarchy in the aftermath of a bruising 4-1 defeat by Leeds.

Last weekend’s heavy loss at Stamford Bridge made it two defeats in a row for the Blues and has led to plenty of criticism of Alonso and his team’s style of play.

Chelsea will bid to get back to winning ways when they travel to face Nottingham Forest at the City Ground in the Premier League on Friday night.

At his pre-match press conference on Thursday, Alonso was asked what conversations he has had with owner Behdad Egbhali and Chelsea’s sporting directors during the club’s recent drop-off in form.

“The focus has been tomorrow [Friday], it’s been the game [against Forest],” he said.

“It has been about showing a strong reaction, showing a competitive reaction, a competitive level that we need for tomorrow, for the rest of the games. That we can do much better, that it was not good enough in the last game.

“That has been the main topic for us, for the team. If you look just on Saturday, we missed not just players, we missed many basics to compete in the game.

“So that’s been clear during the week: talk about how we need to have those basics in football to compete.”

Alonso also revealed that while neither Joao Pedro nor Maxence Lacroix have returned from injury in time to be involved against Forest, Moises Caicedo will be available to play.

It comes after the Ecuador midfielder was forced off in the first half of the Leeds game with a knock. He was later assessed and has been deemed fit for the trip to Forest in a major boost for Chelsea.

#1695. Chelsea injury update: Moises Caicedo, Joao Pedro, Reece James latest news and return dates

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea are set to welcome back a key man ahead of their trip to Nottingham Forest on Friday.

The Blues open up matchday 12 of the Premier League season at the City Ground, looking to bounce back from their 4-1 defeat by Leeds last time out.

Pressure has piled on manager Xabi Alonso after just one win in their last five matches, and they lost one of their star midfielders just 20 minutes into the encounter.

Here is all the latest Chelsea injury news and potential return dates...

The Ecudaorian returned to the starting lineup after picking up a knock over the international break, but was forced off inside 20 minutes at Stamford Bridge at the weekend.

The midfielder went down under challenge from James Justin, but could not continue and was sacrificed prematurely.

Alonso said that their £115m signing from 2023 would need assessment after the game, but he revealed in a fresh update on Thursday that the former Brighton man would be fit for the trip to Forest.

“He is going to be okay for tomorrow,” the Spaniard said.

Star striker Joao Pedro was a surprise absentee for the home defeat by Tottenham last month.

The Brazilian has been out for a whole month with a thigh problem picked up innocuously, missing Brazil duty a fortnight ago.

He has still not returned to full training, according to Alonso, who added a simple “No” when asked if the No9 could return in Nottinghamshire.

Behind the scenes at Chelsea, Standard Sport understands that some are concerned he will not be able to feature for the Blues until the new year.

The England international picked up a knee injury in training last month which he was forced to have minor surgery on.

Standard Sport understands that the right-back will be out for three months, which would mean a return after the turn of the year.

Summer signing Lacroix picked up a hamstring injury in the Carabao Cup penalty defeat by Liverpool.

The Frenchman is not expected to be back in action until the new year, with Alonso keeping his cards close to his chest in his latest update.

“It’s one less week than the last game, so we are closer to the return. But not for this game,” he said.

Dutch international Hato has been suffering with a back problem that he first sustained ahead of the international break.

The versatile defender was thought to be available for the game against Leeds, but Alonso insisted that his recovery would “take a while”.

“Jorrel has a back problem and we need to be patient because it’s going to take a while,” the Spaniard said.

The winger has had an injury-hit spell since joining from Borussia Dortmund in the summer of 2025.

He picked up a nasty ankle issue in England Under-21’s fixture against Kazakhstan, leaving him on crutches after the game.

He has returned to training with his club-mates, and Alonso was positive in his latest update on the forward.

He said: “Jamie Gittens, he’s better. He’s already training with the team but we want to give him more time to come back in the squad.”

#1694. Liverpool injury, suspension list and return dates vs. Everton: Cody Gakpo, Ryan Gravenberch, Victor Munoz latest

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:18, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:18

Liverpool are back in action on Sunday afternoon when they square off against Everton in the Merseyside derby.

Andoni Iraola's side start the next batch of fixtures sitting in fourth position in the Premier League table.

However, although they earned an impressive 3-0 win at Club Brugge in the Champions League in midweek, the Spaniard is dealing with a number of injury issues.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Everton, who are still reeling from their 4-0 defeat at Brentford last time out.

Possible return date: December 2 (vs. Sunderland)

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Manchester United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Having also missed the Club Brugge game, the versatile attacker has already been ruled out of this fixture.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton)

Although Ryan Gravenberch finds himself in a similar position to Gakpo, he has not been conclusively ruled out of this fixture, with Iraola revealing that Liverpool are attempting to 'manage the pain' of his heel issue.

© Imago / Propaganda Photo, David Rawcliffe, Amanda McMaster

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the New Year is still incredibly unlikely.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City)

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton)

Victor Munoz took a heavy knock to his knee against Club Brugge and was subsequently withdrawn. However, after the game, Iraola revealed that the initial pain had subsided, leaving the Spaniard to be assessed ahead of this contest.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

#1693. Vancouver prepared for ‘extremely difficult’ playoff test, says Sorensen

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vancouver Whitecaps boss Jesper Sorensen acknowledged an "extremely difficult" playoff match against Real Salt Lake awaits them on Friday.

The top seed from the Western Conference won Game 1 of the best-of-three series 2-0, with Edier Ocampo and Bruno Caicedo scoring either side of half-time.

The Whitecaps, who reached the MLS Cup showpiece last year, can secure progression to the next round of the 2026 postseason with victory in Game 2 at America First Field.

Vancouver defeated FC Dallas in this round of the MLS Cup playoffs last term in two games, but were taken to penalties in Game 2.

Sorensen believes RSL will pose a serious threat and has urged his side to remember their exploits against Dallas in 2025.

"Game 2 is a tricky one for those who won Game 1; it's really about seeing if you can close it out against a team that plays with desperation, and we've seen how many teams had to go to three games to advance," Sorensen told reporters.

"This is going to be extremely difficult, but we know that we have the experience from last year in Dallas.

"In this league, it can be very difficult playing away. We're going to play up with some altitude, and we're going to play probably in some cold weather.

"It's going to be a different scenario than we played under the other day in BC, and that's what makes this league beautiful as well.

"We're facing a team that has to win this game to stay alive in the season, and we know that it's going to be a bit difficult."

One badge. One team. One club.  #OwnTheSummit https://t.co/7ebj0dMmhr

— Vancouver Whitecaps FC (@WhitecapsFC) November 25, 2026

Sergi Solans has scored 11 goals at home in MLS matches this season (regular season and playoffs).

The only RSL players with more home goals in MLS play in a season (including playoffs) are Alvaro Saborio in 2012 (13) and Robbie Findley in 2009 (12).

Ocampo scored the Whitecaps' opening goal last week, scoring from a shot with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.034.

He has scored three goals in MLS play this season (regular season and playoffs), with two of those having an xG value of 0.035 or lower.

MATCH PREDICTION: VANCOUVER WHITECAPS WIN

Vancouver's 2-0 win over RSL in Game 1 was their fifth straight victory in the fixture. That is Vancouver's second-longest win streak in MLS play against any opponent, trailing only their current six-game run against Sporting Kansas City.

The Whitecaps have won three of their six MLS Cup playoff matches since the beginning of 2025 (D2 L1). That matches Vancouver's win total in their 14 MLS Cup playoff games prior to that (W3 D2 L9).

The Game 1 loss moved RSL's winless streak in the MLS Cup playoffs to 10 straight matches (D6 L4), as the club's last win was in 2021 against Sporting KC.

That is tied for the longest winless streak in MLS playoff history with Minnesota United's current 10-match run that started in 2020.

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea are set to welcome back a key man ahead of their trip to Nottingham Forest on Friday.

The Blues open up matchday 12 of the Premier League season at the City Ground, looking to bounce back from their 4-1 defeat by Leeds last time out.

Pressure has piled on manager Xabi Alonso after just one win in their last five matches, and they lost one of their star midfielders just 20 minutes into the encounter.

Here is all the latest Chelsea injury news and potential return dates...

The Ecudaorian returned to the starting lineup after picking up a knock over the international break, but was forced off inside 20 minutes at Stamford Bridge at the weekend.

The midfielder went down under challenge from James Justin, but could not continue and was sacrificed prematurely.

Alonso said that their £115m signing from 2023 would need assessment after the game, but he revealed in a fresh update on Thursday that the former Brighton man would be fit for the trip to Forest.

“He is going to be okay for tomorrow,” the Spaniard said.

Star striker Joao Pedro was a surprise absentee for the home defeat by Tottenham last month.

The Brazilian has been out for a whole month with a thigh problem picked up innocuously, missing Brazil duty a fortnight ago.

He has still not returned to full training, according to Alonso, who added a simple “No” when asked if the No9 could return in Nottinghamshire.

Behind the scenes at Chelsea, Standard Sport understands that some are concerned he will not be able to feature for the Blues until the new year.

The England international picked up a knee injury in training last month which he was forced to have minor surgery on.

Standard Sport understands that the right-back will be out for three months, which would mean a return after the turn of the year.

#1691. Omar Marmoush hails ‘unbelievable’ Tottenham star as new long-term contract signed

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Omar Marmoush has hailed Luca Williams-Barnett as “unbelievable” and believes the teen sensation has a “very promising future ahead of him”.

Man Utd XI vs Brentford: Confirmed team news and predicted lineup

Marmoush injury update as new Tottenham footage emerges

Choose the right education path for your child

The 18-year-old scored one, and set up another, on his full debut for Tottenham in their 2-0 home win against Ipswich last weekend.

Williams-Barnett has since signed a new deal to commit his future to Spurs until 2031.

“He is unbelievable,” said Marmoush of the Tottenham academy graduate.

“He is a great, great talent and what I like most about him, of course his talent is something that everyone sees, is that he is very brave, too.

“When he came on in his first game, he just took the ball and tried things. He is very direct, tries to beat his opponent and he has a very, very promising future ahead of him.”

Speaking to Sky Sports, Marmoush continued: “He has got it, and you can see that. One of the big traits of a big talent, and a big player, is the personality and the character and that is what stands out most for me, his courage and to be brave.

“As a young lad to come into Spurs’ first team and perform like that is not easy, and just to believe in yourself, and do the actions on your pitch is great. I hope he is enjoying it, and he will have a very, very big future, that’s for sure.”

Marmoush joined Tottenham on a season-long loan from Manchester City at the close of the summer transfer window, to follow Savio, who completed a permanent £85million transfer, out of the Etihad Stadium.

Reflecting on his move to north London, Marmoush, who has played 11 times so far for Roberto De Zerbi’s improving side, continued: “Spurs are one of the biggest clubs in the world and in England.

“They have a big project and lots of ambitions and they are clear in what direction they want to go, and they are building towards that, and both me and Savio have the same in us – a lot of goals that we want to reach and ambitions, too, so it suits us so well at this club.

“We were convinced by the project and we are very happy to be here.

“The boys are very happy. We are beginning to see the work we have put in come to life. The team spirit is very good right now, and we keep looking forward, and keep working.”

Spurs will be aiming to build on their fourth win in five games – which has lifted them to 10th in the Premier League table – when they take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light on Sunday.

#1690. Stevenage vs Blackpool - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 26 Nov 2026 13:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 13:31

Looking to extend their unbeaten run to six matches in all competitions, Stevenage welcome managerless Blackpool to Broadhall Way on Saturday afternoon for the sides' final League One fixture of the month.

Boro followed up a 1-0 victory away to Notts County with a goalless draw against Sheffield Wednesday during the week, while the Seasiders claimed their first point under interim boss Steve Thompson thanks to a late Niall Ennis equaliser in an unlikely draw against Leicester City.

After suffering playoff heartbreak last season, where Stevenage finished sixth before losing to Stockport County in the semi-finals, the Hertfordshire-based club stuck with Alex Revell in the hope that the former striker could lead Boro one step further this time around.

However, after 14 League One matches, Stevenage sit 13th in the table with five wins, five draws and four defeats leaving them on 20 points, six adrift of the playoff places.

Despite that, they remain closer to the top six than the bottom four and have put together some encouraging results as they look to turn their slow start to the season around.

After beginning the month by securing their place in the next round of the FA Cup, Stevenage finished top of their EFL Trophy group thanks to a penalty shootout victory over Fulham Under-21s, before beating Notts County and drawing with recently relegated Sheffield Wednesday.

Their recent run of form has also seen them keep three clean sheets in four matches across all competitions in November, playing a major role in helping them maintain the best defensive record in League One, with no side having conceded fewer than their 13 goals.

Saturday will mark their 15th league outing of the campaign, a fixture that they marked with a 1-0 victory over Peterborough United just over a year ago to move top of the table, highlighting the stark contrast with their performances at the same stage last season.

As for Blackpool, they look set to play their third match under interim manager Thompson, who took charge at Bloomfield Road following the departure of Ian Evatt, who was relieved of his duties after a 57-game spell with the Seasiders.

Evatt left the Lancashire-based club following a 1-0 defeat to AFC Wimbledon, a result that left Blackpool 20th and level on points with teams in the relegation zone.

Thompson, who has previously had three other spells as Blackpool's caretaker manager, oversaw a 2-1 defeat to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic before guiding his side to a 1-1 draw with recently relegated Leicester City.

The stalemate with the Foxes came courtesy of an 84th-minute equaliser from Ennis in a match where the Seasiders had just 22.9% possession and faced 30 shots, but the unlikely point was enough to keep them outside the relegation zone.

Thompson is expected to remain in charge for this weekend's fixture, with Blackpool yet to appoint a permanent successor to Evatt, while Matt Bloomfield and Richie Wellens have both been linked with the vacancy.

Should Blackpool secure what would be just their fourth league win of the season this weekend, they could head into December with a three-point cushion above the drop zone, giving their next permanent manager an opportunity to take charge of a side unbeaten in two matches, although they face a Stevenage team that defeated them both home and away last season.

After drawing at home to Sheffield Wednesday in midweek, Revell will be keen to keep his side unchanged and has the luxury of doing so after his squad came through the match without any fresh injury concerns.

Tommy Setford has played a key role in Stevenage's impressive defensive record, and the 20-year-old goalkeeper is expected to retain his place as he bids to register his fifth clean sheet of the season.

Revell will, however, remain without Jasper Pattenden, Dan Kemp and Jordan Roberts, who are all still sidelined through injury.

For what is likely to be Thompson's third and final match in charge of Blackpool, the former midfielder will once again be without several first-team players.

A sickness bug kept Bailey Peacock-Farrell, Josh Bowler and Finley Munroe out of recent matches, but all three returned for the clash with the Foxes and are expected to feature again this weekend.

Dale Taylor, defenders Josh Earl, Fraser Horsfall and Michael Ihiekwe, as well as captain George Honeyman, are all likely to remain unavailable for the trip to Hertfordshire.

Having scored his second goal of the season after coming off the bench last time out, Ennis is likely to be rewarded with a starting place and could replace either Dion Charles or Jerry Yates.

Setford; Vancooten, Casey, Piergianni, Earley; Phillips, Thompson; Sanderson, Broggio, Patterson; Magennis

Peacock-Farrell; Lyons, Casey, Ashworth, Munroe; Niskanen, Brown, Morgan, Hamilton; Ennis, Charles

With one of the best defensive side's in the English Football League meeting a team who have struggled to score on a regular basis, we see this one going only one way.

We expect the Seasiders' struggles to continue with Boro making it four unbeaten in the league and closing out November with a sixth win of the season.

#1689. Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim

Bruno Fernandes missed a penalty for the second successive pre-season friendly as Manchester United were beaten 4-2 by former head coach Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan.

Fernandes, who rolled a spot-kick wide in a shoot-out against Leeds in midweek, was gifted the chance to open his pre-season account in Wroclaw, Poland.

His effort was on target this time, but Milan keeper Lorenzo Torriani dived to his right to beat the shot away.

Fernandes did at least get an assist, taking the second-minute corner which was powerfully headed home by Harry Maguire to give United the lead.

Amorim’s Milan equalised after a defensive mix-up allowed Gonçalo Ramos to break into the area and square for Samuel Chukwueze to roll home.

United were awarded their penalty just before half-time after Koni De Winter tugged back Youri Tielemans, but Torriani guessed correctly to leave Fernandes frustrated.

United retook the lead after Patrick Dorgu pounced on a loose backpass from Filippo Terracciano, but Milan equalised again when Chukwueze’s wayward shot was poked in by Alphadjo Cissè at the far post.

Marcus Rashford, who was frozen out by Amorim and loaned out to Aston Villa and then Barcelona, came on as a substitute on the hour for his first United appearance since returning from Spain.

But Milan went ahead in the 68th minute when Chukwueze’s cross was headed home by Ramos, and three minutes later former Chelsea midfielder Ruben Loftus-Cheek raced through to hit the fourth and cap a performance that underlines United’s need for reinforcements before their season starts in earnest next Saturday, away at Hull City.

Manchester United (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Mazraoui (Dalot 61), Maguire, Heaven (Martinez 61), Shaw; Tielemans, Santos (Mainoo 61); Diallo (Lacey 61), Fernandes, Dorgu (Rashford 61); Cunha (Mbeumo 61). Subs Zirkzee, Yoro, J Fletcher, T Fletcher, Amass, Collyer, Mee (g), Heath (g), Gabriel. Booked Dorgu.

AC Milan (3-4-2-1) Torriani; Terracciano (Gila 60), Winter (Vladimirov 84), Pavlovic (Diawara 84); Chukwueze, Musah (Ricci 76), Jashari (Modric 60), Estupinan (Bartesaghi 61); Loftus-Cheek (Comotto 84), Cisse (Saelemaekers 60); Ramos (Camarda 75). Subs Pittarella (g), Bouyer (g). Booked Estupinan.

Goals Chukwueze (37), Cisse (57), Ramos (68), Loftus-Cheek (71).

That six-time Champions League winner Luka Modric raised the trophy with the one hand said everything you need to know about this moment...

Aug 30: Manchester United vs Ipswich Town

Sep 13: Manchester United vs Manchester City

United’s pre-season ends in defeat. A wretched second half proves their undoing as Amorim’s Milan score four. Worth reminding that United led this match, twice.

Milan are playing keep-ball in these latter stages and although Mainoo regains possession, his attempt to play forward is cut out and Modric’s outside-of-the-foot pass finds Comotto, who heads straight at Lammens.

Four minutes of added time to be played...

United now raining crosses down on Milan’s box but Torriani equal to it every time.

For the second time this afternoon, Shaw directs a lovely ball into Fernandes’ path in behind Milan’s back line, but the Portugal international can’t bring it under his spell.

Martinez has added a little bit of urgency to United’s build-up. Mbeumo tries to feed Shaw down the line but the ball is cut out.

More substitutions... Diawara, Vladimirov and Comotto enter the field of play in place of Pavlovic, De Winter and Loftus-Cheek.

Big chance for Rashford! Martinez lofts a fantastic ball over the top but Rashford is not quite able to bring it under his spell, with Torriani and De Winter combing to clear their lines.

Milan are now sitting off, settling into a back five as they look to preserve their advantage. Fernandes, Tielemans and Dalot combine well but such has been United’s fortunes this afternoon, the ball ricochets off the referee and play is halted.

Good work from Rashford in the corner to regain possession, but his ball into the box is not picked up by a team-mate.

More changes... Ramos and Musah make way for Camarda and Ricci.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 4 (Loftus-Cheek) No sooner had the players returned after the second-half hydration break then Milan exploit United’s exposed left side (again). Ramos sends Loftus-Cheek through and the midfielder composes himself before bending the ball around Lammens.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 3 (Ramos) That’s too easy. United fail to learn their lesson, Shaw not getting tight enough to Chukwueze and the winger’s cross is met by new signing Ramos, who powers a header back across goal and past Lammens.

Loftus-Cheek and Ramos are doing a good job of cutting off the pass into United’s midfield in their build-up phase.

Rashford (who makes his first United appearance in almost two years), Lacey, Dalot, Mbeumo, Mainoo and Martinez replace Dorgu, Amad, Mazraoui, Cunha, Santos and Heaven.

For Milan, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Gila and Modric are on for Cisse, Estupinan, Terracciano and Jashari

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 2 (Cisse) United have set a higher defensive line so far this half, with their front line pressing with more intensity to avoid the ball over the top. However Chukwueze is able to find space around the sides, coming in off the right and curling an effort goalwards which Cisse turns in at the far post. There are calls for offside, but with no VAR here, the goal stands.

Milan win a free-kick some 25 yards out after Fernandes clips Estupinan. Teenager Cisse steps up and fires straight into the United wall. Was always going to be difficult to trouble Lammens from there.

Manchester United 2 AC Milan 1 (Dorgu) United wisely decide to keep hold of the ball for a while, the midfield three rotating to disrupt Milan’s out-of-possession shape and open up passing lanes. A Milan throw-in from the right-back berth is precedes an awful backpass by Terracciano which is pounced on by Dorgu who curls the ball beyond Torriani.

United have looked bright in the opening moments of this half. They win a free-kick midway into Milan’s half. The ball is delivered to the back post and, after some 18-yard-box pinball, a relieved Torriano pounces on it.

Both teams remain unchanged as the second 45 minutes begin.

All square at the break. Tough to know what to make of that half – United looked solid enough and could have taken a lead into the interval had Fernandes converted his penalty, but they failed to create a wealth of clear-cut chances. It will be interesting to see how Carrick approaches this second half.

Milan have enjoyed just a tick over two-thirds of possession, which United have contributed to in part through some lackadaisical passing.

Fernandes misses a spot-kick for the second time in two friendlies! Here, Torriani guesses correctly, diving to his right to palm Fernandes’ strike away.

De Winter brings down Tielemans inside the box after Terracciano loses the ball attempting to play out from the back.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 1 (Chukwueze) It’s all a bit messy. Jashari causes Maguire and Santos to crash into each other (Kaka at Old Trafford, anyone?) off a throw-in, Ramos taking over with the United pair out of commission. He finds Chukwueze who finishes the move off at the far post.

The match becomes stretched momentarily as Pavlovic, the centre-back, marauds forward, setting the ball to Estupinan who delivers another dangerous cross from the left, which Lammens does well to claim.

Santos clips Loftus-Cheek near the byline and the referee awards Milan a free-kick. Chukwueze cuts the ball back to an unmarked Jashari on the edge of the box, but his side-footed effort flies wide.

Milan supporters unfurl a banner paying tribute to the late, great Franco Baresi, who passed away on July 31 aged 66.

Hermosa bandera a Franco Baresi.QUE EN PAZ DESCANSE, LEYENDA DEL FÚTBOL 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/fvE48nKVSs

United have picked their moments to press. Santos, who has enjoyed a wonderful pre-season, is a little too overzealous in his attempts to regain possession and gives away a foul. But the intent is correct.

Shaw floats a delightful ball over the top for Fernandes to gallop on to. The Portuguese steals in ahead of De Winter but cannot find the target with his weaker left foot.

Cisse escapes the clutches of Mazraoui down the left and fires a shot (more likely a mis-hit cross) straight into the gloves of Lammens.

United finally get their foot on the ball, but Heaven attempts an ambitious cross-field pass and possession goes back to the Italians.

A Mexican wave has already begun. We’re only 21 minutes in...

Carrick’s side continue to sit off, allowing Milan to keep hold of the ball. Cisse works in from the left, playing a neat one-two with Ramos before his curled strike sails well over.

A period of extended possession for Milan, United dropping into a compact 4-4-2 mid-block. Estupinan rains in a dangerous cross from the left and the ball falls to Loftus-Cheek, whose effort is expertly saved by the right boot of Lammens.

Estupinan goes into the book after pulling Amad’s shirt as he looked to dart in behind after Tielemans had played a dangerous through-ball. Might possibly have been the last man?

Tielemans cedes possession to the busy Jashari just outside his own box, the Swiss midfielder moving the ball on to Loftus-Cheek who fires a shot straight at Lammens.

Amad picks Pavlovic’s pocket and the Milan centre-half is forced to concede a corner. United unable to score from this one.

Milan are indeed in Amorim’s preferred 3-4-2-1 formation. They circulate the ball in front of United’s first line of pressure in an attempt to calm things down.

Manchester United 1 AC Milan 0 (Maguire) Fernandes delivers an inswinger from the left and Maguire is there to meet it at the back post, striding past Musa to plant a header past Torriani.

United make a fast start, Dorgu flashing a cross-cum-shot across the face of goal. Torriani gets a fingertip to it and thte ball goes behind for a corner.

Szymon Marciniak, the experienced Polish referee, gets us under way. Milan send the ball back to goalkeeper Torriani.

The players emerge from the tunnel, United debuting their lovely new cream third kit and Milan in their traditional red-and-black home colours. Smoke machines and pyrotechnics add to the atmosphere in Wroclaw...

We are almost ready to go. Let us know your match predictions and thoughts on United’s prospects this season in the comments section beneath this blog.

Manchester United defeated Leeds United on penalties to hoist the mighty Boyle Sports Cup at Croke Park. The match, a 1-1 draw, was brought to an abrupt end after five young pitch invaders ran to the middle of the field to take selfies with Bruno Fernandes. In the shoot-out it was James Justin who missed the “decisive” spot-kick, paving the way for Noussair Mazraoui to win it for United.

Marcus Rashford is on the bench this afternoon and could make his first United appearance since his cameo in a Europa League win over Viktoria Plzen in December 2024. He was frozen out under Amorim and has since been loaned to Aston Villa and Barcelona, but his Old Trafford future under Carrick remains unclear.

Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can push for the Premier League title, but has underlined the urgent need for signings.

The United head coach has taken heart from his squad’s promising preparations for the new campaign and, speaking at their Co Kildare summer base, he explained why he was confident they could build on last season’s third-place finish.

Carrick has been thrilled to hear United’s players discussing what they might achieve and has dared supporters to dream that they can get closer to last year’s champions Arsenal. But he is also a realist and recognises he is not blessed with options.

So far United have added Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, a reserve goalkeeper, but their £83.3m spend is significantly less than what newly promoted clubs Ipswich Town (£109.4m) and Coventry City (£92.2m) have invested in their squads.

Amorim’s side have gone intercontinental this summer, travelling from Scotland to Indonesia, via Australia, before arriving in Poland for the last of their four pre-season games.

In memory of Franco Baresi 🇮🇹♾️ pic.twitter.com/ULAJRjxDvE

Manchester United Lammens; Mazraoui, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Tielemans, Santos, Fernandes; Amad, Dorgu; Cunha

Subs Heath, Mee, Amass, Dalot, Martínez, Yoro, Collyer, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Mainoo, Gabriel, Lacey, Mbeumo, Rashford, Zirkzee

AC Milan Torriani; Terracciano, De Winter, Pavlović; Chukwueze, Jashari, Musah, Estupiñán; Loftus-Cheek, Cissè; Ramos

Subs Bouyer, Pittarella, Gila, Diawara, Vladimirov, Ricci, Saelemaekers, Bartesaghi, Modrić, Comotto, Camarda

At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Welcome to live coverage of Manchester United’s final pre-season match, against AC Milan in Wroclaw, Poland. Michael Carrick’s side will look to apply the finishing touches to a promising summer on the pitch, which has included victories over Rosenborg and Atlético Madrid, plus a draw against European champions Paris St-Germain. The team will fly back to Manchester with the big ones, the ones they have always wanted – the Snapdragon Cup and the Boyle Sports Cup – in tow.

At the Tarczynski Stadium there will be a reunion with former manager Ruben Amorim, who was appointed AC Milan’s head coach in June, five months after being sacked by United. Following a frustrating season under Massimiliano Allegri in which Milan fell out of the Champions League spots on the final day, the Rossoneri said Amorim would bring a “modern dominant tactical approach”. His methods failed to cut through at Old Trafford, though, during a tumultuous 14-month reign which finally ended after the Portuguese “blew up” during a heated meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox. At Milan, Amorim has persisted with the 3-4-2-1 formation that was doomed at United.

Carrick made clear this week that United must strengthen if they are to challenge for titles. So far the club have brought in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Karl Darlow, but they are still in the market for a left-back and another midfielder. The future of Marcus Rashford has also been a topic of conversation among United fans. The forward has not played for his boyhood club since December 2024 but has joined up with his team-mates in Poland and it remains to be seen if he features in Carrick’s forward planning.

Kobbie Mainoo, who did not play a minute at this summer’s World Cup, and Lisandro Martínez have also joined up with the team this week and could be handed their first minutes of pre-season having been named in the matchday squad. For Milan, new signing Gonçalo Ramos – bought from PSG for £63m – will make his first appearance in the famous red and black.

#1688. MN: Milan injury list up to nine as Bartesaghi ruled out of Olympiacos trip – the situation

AC Milan will be without another defender in Greece tomorrow, with news emerging about Davide Bartesaghi being absent for the clash.

In the past 24 hours, Milan have had to deal with several injury problems. Luka Modric was ruled out last night, whilst Francesco Camarda didn’t take part in today’s training session.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Before this, Ruben Amorim’s squad was already looking short – an issue which most have felt was the case since before the summer – and now it’s gotten shorter again, somehow.

According to MilanNews, the Rossoneri will also be without Davide Bartesaghi, who is suffering from a bout of peritendinitis. The young Italian – going off brief searches – could be out for two weeks to six at most, but there’s no more information offered on the issue and its severity.

Of course, the best-case scenario is that it’s a precautionary absence and he’s back for this weekend’s game. However, there’s no information on the matter just yet.

All that is known, though, is that the Diavolo are now up to nine injuries at this moment, with Bartesaghi joining Samuel Chukwueze, Matteo Gabbia, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers, Strahinja Pavlovic, Modric, Camarda and Pietro Terracciano.

It’s a pretty brutal list, indeed and it makes you realise how limited Milan are on the flanks, which is perhaps why another left-back could be signed in January.

#1687. ‘No one can chat s***’: Tottenham star defends Cole Palmer amid Chelsea criticism

Tosin Adarabioyo has said that “no-one can chat s***” about his former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer despite the England international’s struggles this season.

Palmer has scored five times in his 13 appearances across the Premier League and Carabao Cup this term, adding three assists in the top flight.

The England international has also failed to force his way into Thomas Tuchel’s plans on the international stage, having been snubbed for the World Cup squad last summer.

He also missed out on the Nations League cohorts as the Three Lions secured their place in the knockout stages next year with a 3-2 win over Spain earlier this month.

Now, Tottenham defender Tosin has defended his ex-club-mate amid Chelsea’s dip in form, with the Blues suffering a 4-1 defeat to Leeds over the weekend.

Xabi Alonso’s side have won just once in their last five matches, falling to eighth in the table.

“No one can chat s*** about Cole,” Tosin said.

“For me, he's one of the best players I've ever seen. You can say what you want. Honestly, you guys can say what you want. He's a top level player. He will continue to get better.”

Tosin admitted that he was surprised at Tuchel’s neglect of Palmer for England duty, hailing the attacking midfielder as “the best No 10 in the Premier League.”

The England boss had alleged that Palmer had shown a lack of commitment to his national team, but Tosin laughed off the suggestion.

“False, false, false,” he continued. “I know Cole's dreams, his aspirations. So, yeah, it's completely false.”

#1686. ‘One of the best’: Sandro Tonali issues verdict on Tottenham star after superb Ipswich showing

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Sandro Tonali has hailed Tottenham team-mate Destiny Udogie as “one of the best” left-backs.

The Italian pair were already familiar with one another before Tonali’s big-money move to north London from Newcastle United in the summer for a fee worth £100million.

They had first played together in at Under-21 level on the international stage, before reuniting for the senior Azzurri side and at club level.

Udogie, who was told by manager Roberto De Zerbi what he must do to start more games, was given the nod from the off against Ipswich Town last time out, as Spurs won 2-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The left-back impressed behind Luca Williams-Barnett, with the young star netting his first goal for the club on his first senior start.

Udogie, meanwhile, was making just his fifth start of the campaign amid injury problems.

He has also had to contend with former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson arriving to add competition in his position after Djed Spence’s departure for Inter Milan.

On Udogie, Tonali told Stadium Astro: "He's a lovely guy. He's I think he's one of the best left wing[-backs]. He has to work every day now. He has a little bit of a problem with injuries, but I think he's a good guy for us.

"I think he played one of the best games against Manchester [United], and he pushes up like a high winger, and I love him because he's always happy.

"If you win, he's happy; if you lose, he's happy. If you have a bad day, he's happy, and I think when I look at him, I'm happy."

#1685. Manchester United dealt transfer blow as ‘January target’ signs new contract

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has shut down all rumours of a Leeds United exit by signing a new contract at Elland Road.

The striker had been linked with a move away from the Yorkshire club - with several outlets identifying him as a potential target for Manchester United - but he will remain a White after penning a new two-and-a-half-year deal.

The No9 has spent the past two seasons at Leeds, joining Daniel Farke’s side upon their return to the Premier League last term.

He has established himself as the club’s first-choice striker since his free transfer move after his contract at Everton expired at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

The England international has forced his way into Thomas Tuchel’s plans for the most recent Nations League games, and he could well have a chance to impress up top with Harry Kane sidelined after tearing his ankle ligaments.

Calvert-Lewin netted 15 goals in his first season in a Leeds shirt, and he has six strikes in 13 matches so far this term.

His hot run of goalscoring form has seen him linked with a move to Old Trafford, where new manager Mauricio Pochettino is thought to be keen on reinforcing his attack after injuries to Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford.

Calvert-Lewin was one of the names that was reportedly on the Red Devils’ shortlist ahead of the January transfer window, but his decision to sign a new contract at Elland Road will come as a major blow to Pochettino as he looks to shape United’s squad in his image.

#1684. Liverpool transfer news: Who is Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, the 16-year-old Senegalese phenomenon expected in 2028?

By Axel Clody | 26 Nov 2026 13:28

Liverpool may have found their next great Senegalese talent. The Premier League club have reportedly reached a verbal agreement to sign Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, a 16-year-old winger who currently plays for Diambars.

However, Liverpool fans will have to be patient, as the young Senegalese cannot move to England until January 2028.

The news was revealed by Fabrizio Romano, who confirmed that a verbal agreement exists between the two parties.

Having already been given a trial by Liverpool in the summer of 2025, Ndiaye reportedly convinced the club's scouts, who have now secured an option on his arrival. Born on 31 December 2009, he will turn 18 at the end of 2027, which is a requirement for a move to England.

??? Liverpool have verbally agreed deal to sign 16 year old winger Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, here we go! Senegalese talent to join in January 2028, when he turns 18. Ndiaye was already at Liverpool on trial in 2025 and ready to become #LFC player for future. https://t.co/DrBIfNkPJR

A product of Diambars, one of the most renowned academies in Senegal, Sidy Barhama Ndiaye plays mainly on the right but can also operate on the left. He first caught the eye at the 2025 Under-17 Africa Cup of Nations, played when he was only 15, before continuing to progress with Senegal's youth teams.

His main qualities are his pace, his explosiveness and his ability to beat an opponent one on one. Very direct when receiving the ball, he likes to provoke, accelerate and create openings. He also has a degree of efficiency in the final ball, as he again demonstrated at the Under-17 World Cup.

During Senegal's 9-0 thrashing of Cuba, the young winger scored one goal and provided two assists. The performance helped to boost his reputation among European observers and scouts.

The comparison with Sadio Mane comes naturally around the young Senegalese.

Besides his origins, Ndiaye shares with his illustrious elder an attacking profile built on pace, penetration and the ability to make a difference on the wings. And if Liverpool, who benefited from Mane's talent for six seasons, complete the deal, that comparison will be unavoidable.

However, there is still a long way to go before he can be expected to play at Anfield. Between now and January 2028, Ndiaye will have to continue to progress at Diambars and confirm the promise shown with Senegal's youth teams.

Liverpool, for their part, have already taken a position on a player they want to integrate into their long-term project.

#1683. Chelsea boss Alonso reveals Fofana apology after penalty joke

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Xabi Alonso revealed Wesley Fofana has apologised to his Chelsea team-mates for giving an interview in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss against Liverpool.

Fofana missed the decisive spot-kick as the Blues were beaten 6-5 on spot-kicks at Anfield in the round of 16 in the EFL Cup, at the end of October.

The centre-back blazed his effort high into the stands, and he subsequently told YouTube personality Zack Nani: "I knew I wasn't a good penalty taker to begin with!"

Those comments attracted fierce criticism from sections of Chelsea's fanbase, particularly with Alonso's team sitting eighth in the Premier League following back-to-back defeats against Sunderland and Leeds United.

But ahead of Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest, the Blues boss insisted the matter was now considered closed.

Asked if he had spoken to Fofana about the interview, Alonso said: "Absolutely. We have addressed that with him and, for sure, it was unfortunate.

"He has apologised. He knows it was not right in the moment, it was not right, the content.

"We are here to take things seriously and he has said it is not going to be repeated, and we know that it is something we don't want, these kinds of things.

"They are not going to be repeated, for sure."

Happy birthday, Xabi! https://t.co/pEjttfS5ou

— Chelsea FC (@ChelseaFC) November 25, 2026

Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), and among ever-present clubs, only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues in that same span (23).

This season, Chelsea's Premier League games have seen more goals than those containing any other side (40 – 20 for, 20 against).

This is the earliest point in a league campaign (11 games) where the Blues have both scored and conceded 20+ goals since 1960-61 (eight games).

Asked what he put Chelsea's struggles down to, Alonso said: "There are many reasons. Football reasons, things that we can't afford to do.

"The basics in football are so important to compete at this level. If you don't have those, you play as we did.

"The idea and the goal and the work and the talks have all been focused on that direction, to show a good game and to compete much better tomorrow."

Chelsea are unbeaten in their last five away league games against Forest (W4 D1), with their current run of three consecutive victories being their best ever at the City Ground.
