#1682. Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal told Kroupi decision; Liverpool done deal; Man Utd twist; Chelsea latest

The January transfer window is approaching fast, with Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham all striving to get some early signings over the line. Arsenal have been told Bournemouth’s decision over selling top target Eli Junior Kroupi, while they continue to scout Antonio Nusa amid new links to the likes of Carlos Forbs and Tornike Kvaratskhelia.

Liverpool have agreed a deal to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye, while they are also said to be contemplating a surprise return to Anfield for Jarell Quansah. Manchester United are looking at both Calvin Bassey and Nathan Collins as they try to strengthen their dreadful defence, with a new striker also high on Mauricio Pochettino’s shortlist with a rumoured £50million budget - including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has agreed a new contract with Leeds.

Chelsea are renewing their push to win the fierce battle for Alex Scott as Paris Saint-Germain pursue Estevao, while Tottenham have signed former West Ham youngster Isaac Allen ahead of Arsenal as they also scout Vangelis Pavlidis and Hakan Calhanoglu. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below!

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has shut down all rumours of a Leeds United exit by signing a new contract at Elland Road.

The striker had been linked with a move away from the Yorkshire club - with several outlets identifying him as a potential target for Manchester United - but he will remain a White after penning a new two-and-a-half-year deal.

Paris Saint-Germain could push to sign Chelsea star Estevao or rival Arsenal for Antonio Nusa, reports claim.

Reigning back-to-back European champions PSG are on the lookout for further attacking reinforcements in the January transfer window as they seek to ensure another trophy-laden campaign under Luis Enrique.

According to Diario AS in Spain, the French giants are interested in offering the little-used Estevao an escape route from Stamford Bridge.

The Brazilian is said to feature on a shortlist along with Arsenal target Nusa - of RB Leipzig - and Bayern Munich’s Luis Diaz.

Jarell Quansah could make a surprise return to Liverpool.

The versatile defender has continued to flourish since leaving Anfield for Bayer Leverkusen in a £35m deal in the summer of 2025, impressing in the Bundesliga and becoming a favoured option of England boss Thomas Tuchel.

That has led to reported interest in a swift Premier League comeback from the likes of Arsenal and Chelsea.

According to TEAMtalk, Liverpool are keeping a close eye on Quansah’s progress in Germany and haven’t ruled out activating a buy-back clause that is valid until next summer and believed to be valued at just over £50m.

Teenage defender Isaac Allen has confirmed that he has joined Tottenham after leaving rivals West Ham in the summer, writes Sam Tabuteau.

In August, reports claimed that Spurs had beaten Arsenal to Allen’s signature, and the 15-year-old has now announced the move on social media.

The England U15s captain wrote in a post on Instagram: “Happy to be signed with Tottenham.”

Allen, who can operate either at centre-back or in defensive midfield, is regarded as one of the most promising young talents in England and his arrival continues Spurs’ busy youth recruitment strategy.

Tottenham look to be keeping a close eye on Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Spurs are known to be on the lookout for a new forward ahead of the January transfer window to help boost Roberto De Zerbi’s inconsistent attack.

They have been linked with a swoop for Pavlidis for some time now, with Portuguese outlet Record reporting that they dispatched scouts to watch the Greek international in action again this week.

Arsenal appear to have a new transfer target in Carlos Forbs.

The 22-year-old winger has made quite an impact in Belgium with Club Brugge and already has three senior international appearances for Portugal under his belt.

Forbs previously played for Ajax and spent time on loan at Wolves during the 2024/25 campaign, while he played the full 90 minutes for Brugge in their 3-0 home Champions League defeat by Liverpool last night.

Football Insider claim that Arsenal have added him to their list of left-sided attacking targets before the January window, but Brugge have apparently told them already that he will not be sold mid-season.

Manchester United’s hopes of signing Dominic Calvert-Lewin look to be all but over.

The England international was thought to remain high on the transfer shortlist at Old Trafford ahead of their first window under new boss Mauricio Pochettino, who is focusing on the addition of a new striker in January as well as attempting to fix his much-criticised defence as he is handed an initial budget of around £50m.

But according to The Athletic, Calvert-Lewin has now agreed terms on a lucrative contract extension with rivals Leeds that will keep him at Elland Road until the summer of 2029.

There’s a done deal at Liverpool, who are said to have agreed to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye.

Currently 16, Ndiaye plays for Diambars FC in Senegal, but has impressed for his country during the ongoing Under-17 World Cup in Qatar.

Fabrizio Romano claims that he will join Liverpool when he turns 18 in January 2028, having already spent time on trial at Anfield last year.

Other outlets claim that it is only an “option” for Liverpool to sign Ndiaye and does not have to be triggered.

Arsenal are said to have been informed of Bournemouth’s decision over selling top transfer target Eli Junior Kroupi in January.

The French striker appears to have moved to the very top of Mikel Arteta’s shortlist in north London, and may well have been pursued in the summer were it not for an ill-timed foot injury that required surgery and ruled him out for months.

However, talkSPORT claim that Bournemouth will refuse to sell the £100m-rated forward in the New Year, with Kroupi also said to prefer a switch to Paris Saint-Germain over Arsenal.

Liverpool have successfully negotiated the option to sign Senegal wonderkid Sidy Barhama Ndiaye once he turns 18.

Ndiaye, currently 16, trialled with Liverpool’s academy in the summer of 2025 and now has a clear pathway to Merseyside.

Per reports from The Athletic, the Reds have pipped a number of European rivals to get right of first refusal for his signing in January 2028.

English clubs cannot sign players from overseas until they have turned 18, which Ndiaye will do on New Year’s Eve in 2027.

#1681. Alguacil looks at Milan’s favouritism, respect and playing to win: “Life or death match”

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

For Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

“What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

“We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

“We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”

“Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

“Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

“He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”

#1680. Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City

Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Another notable incident was Martin Odegaard, not long after he had glossed a fabulous display with a third goal, sprinting 30 yards to spook Gianluigi Donnarumma and make the Italian hurry his clearance. The victory was good, the trophy was nice, but the energy heartened Arteta more than anything.

“They are really good examples,” Arteta said. “The way the team tracks back is unbelievable, especially when, fitness-wise, we aren’t there yet. We had desire and composure on the ball. When you put your soul and your heart into every action, this is what happens. We want to do it again.

“The desire comes from them thinking: ‘I want to live that moment again. I want to have all the moments again and I want them to be even bigger.’ We know what it is going to take. We have never done it [retain the Premier League] at this football club. We know it will demand something special.”

You could flip that and say it will take something special from the chasers. George Graham and Arsène Wenger could never hold on to the biggest prize during their reigns and you must return to Herbert Chapman, in Arsenal’s thriving 1930s, to find the only manager who went back-to-back.

It can feel premature (and can be foolish) to go out on a limb before the first weekend, but there was just something about them that felt different. Often in the past they have been overtly tentative when playing City, but they came out of their corner this time swinging – and they landed.

Enzo Maresca revealed afterwards that he “really didn’t like” how Arsenal had scored their first goal and that was putting it mildly, as there were 10 passes – broken only by the ball bouncing off Elliott Anderson’s shins – before Myles Lewis-Skelly ushered Calafiori into wreak havoc.

You had to go back to 1968, when City played West Brom, to find the last first-minute goal – City’s Bobby Owen was the scorer that day – and how Calafiori enjoyed it, shaking his fist in delight as Arsenal’s noisy fans reminded everyone of their status.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Here was a rude awakening for Anderson, City’s new £116m man. He was ever so slightly off the pace and that allowed Lewis-Skelly to slip a beautiful ball in behind the FA Cup winners’ defence and invite Calafiori to do the rest, which he did with assurance.

When Maresca watches back the video, he will see Abdukodir Khusanov sleeping and Phil Foden failing to press, but that should not detract from the quality of Arsenal’s interchanging – and it should also make whoever is hawking Lewis-Skelly around to clubs to think again. Why would he leave this?

It should not have been the case that a goal so soon should have governed how the game progressed, but that is exactly what happened as Arsenal completely dominated. Whenever they lost possession, they recovered it as a matter of urgency. Without Pep Guardiola on the touchline, City were like Samson after Delilah shaved his hair, devoid of all power.

City, in contrast to their opponents, showed a complete lack of desire and the second goal arrived when Odegaard was allowed time to flip a ball to the back post, where new boy Tzolis was arriving. The Greek headed back into the six-yard area and Kai Havertz did the rest.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Arsenal were criticised – fairly – during their title-winning campaign for being too physical and relying on gamesmanship, but if Havertz and Odegaard can stay fit for a prolonged period, the difference in style will be like night and day.

Throw in Tzolis, who was tricky and dynamic in Cardiff, to the mix and there will be another enhancement. He looks considerably better than Gabriel Martinelli, with more end product, and Bukayo Saka will do more down the right than Noni Madueke, who started here.

Maresca knew, with his team lacking fitness, that it would be difficult to overhaul the deficit once they had gone two goals behind but, really, he was lucky that Arsenal did not administer a genuine hiding which, at one stage, seemed as though they might.

Goal number three arrived just after the interval, again Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis were involved, combining to enable Odegaard to waltz into the area, hoodwinking Donnarumma so he sat down before sliding a contemptuous finish beyond him.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Had they gone through the gears, there could have been more, but it didn’t matter. What Arsenal showed was far more significant than a couple of more goals when the game was being disrupted by substitutions. The tackles, the running, energy and commitment – that is what brought Arteta joy.

“I’m extremely happy with the performance, the result and winning the first trophy,” Arteta purred.

You would be brave to say it will be their last.

Arsenal (4-2-3-1) Raya 7; White 7, Mosquera 7, Gabriel 7, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie h-t): Guimarães 7 (Rice h-t), Lewis-Skelly 8 (Zublimendi 75); Madueke 6 [Saka 60], Odegaard 8 (Eze 84), Tzolis 7; Havertz 7 (Gyokeres 75). Booked Calafiori, Odegaard. Subs Kepa (g), Merino, Dowman.

Goals: Calafiori (1), Havertz (28), Odegaard (48).

Manchester City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma 5; Khusnaov 5, Dias 5, Gvardiol 5, O’Reilly 5; Anderson 5 (Lewis 60), Kovacic 5 (Gonzalez 79); Semenyo 6, Foden 5 (Cherki 60), Doku 6 (Grealish h-t); Haaland 5 (Marmoush 53). Booked Gvardiol, Foden. Subs Ait-Nouri, Reis, Nunes, Rulli (g).

It’s really sad. I’ve been fighting with the Premier League to extend & accommodate more players in the squad. They deserve to be in the squad, so hopefully we can change that rule.

I think the goal we conceded after 25 seconds unfortunately affected the game in that moment. I think after the goal, the reaction was quite good before they scored the second one, we had three or four chances to score and draw the game but unfortunately we conceded the second one and it became more complicated.

A really, really good performance so early in the season. To play at the level we did and the desire we showed, I just told them that I really enjoyed watching them.

He makes good decisions when a lot of people rush things, he did it twice in tight areas and two goals.

I joined midway [in pre-season]. This is the third game since I have been back. The feeling has been good. Today is frustrating, and it is a final that we all wanted to win. If there is a lesson to be learnt in the final, let it be this one, as there’s a lot more coming. It is a positive energy.

The feeling of a lot of work to put into. It’s part of any transition for things to be not so perfect in the beginning. You need to push through, you need to communicate, and make things work between us. I feel we’re in a very good way, but we need to keep on working. There’s going to be lots of challenges along the way.

Appears to the Community Shield trophy, which caught him a glancing blow to the face.

Trophy lift gone wrong, featuring Declan Rice 😂🏆📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ghmGZJDxka

The players judge the correct level of celebration judiciously, but then Mikel Merino cracks and starts spraying the champagne. While it is a semi-competitive game, Arteta and his players will point out that they earned their place in the fixture by winning the league.

Arsenal start the season with silverware 🏆The Community Shield belongs to the Gunners!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M6GqsGkRF7

What happens to them? I’m not sure the winners’ medals would take pride of place, let alone the silvers.

We played some brilliant football. Great performance and a great way to start the season.

I always want to help the team as much possible with goals and assists. I want to score more goals.

We showed our level today. We’re showed we’re ready. We’re serious and we want to do it again.

We want to attack it. We want to do it again. When you get a taste of how nice it is you want to do it again.

The league champions kick-off the domestic season with a resounding and stylish victory. Shades of 1998 and 2004 when they swept Manchester United aside in this fixture as title winners, only to fail to defend the crown in the season that followed. So maybe it is unwise to make bold forecasts, but it could not have gone better for Arteta. Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Tzolis caught the eye, and Arsenal had their usual solidarity defensively. City just completely off the pace, one to write off and move on.

Marmoush is feeling his hip after a challenge by Mosquera. City have a free-kick wide right. Gabriel heads away Grealish’s delivery in trademark fashion.

Just three minutes of added time to play. No City player is there to meet Cherki’s low cross and White can clear under little pressure.

Rice uncharacteristically caught dallying in midfield but City cannot capitalise. Cheers from the Arsenal fans as Saka wins a throw in from Grealish. Marmoush with a chance to run at Mosquera, but his touch is far too heavy.

City have a free-kick in a crossing position right of centre, but many of their fans are now packing up their banners and heading for the exits. If they haven’t already. Cherki’s delivery is poor, and Rice heads away.

Odegaard with a loose touch, and a yellow card for catching Grealish with the resulting challenge. That was the Arsenal captain’s last action of the game, he is replaced by Eberechi Eze. Odegaard has looked back to his 2024 past today, Eze’s best chance of a start might be from the left.

City’s best move of the second half: Cherki gliding through the challenges and finding Semenyo with a lovely reverse pass, and his shot was drilled towards the far corner. Sharp reflexes by Raya to plunge to his right and save.

Nico Gonzalez replaces Kovacic as Maresca makes his sixth change of the second half. The game has felt like a training exercise since Odegaard’s third goal with the occasional flash of quality.

Chance for Saka! Cracking low cross from Hincapie, but Saka sweeps over from near the penalty spot. Too much on it as he tried to help the ball on its way.

Better tempo to Manchester City’s football, and Gvardiol has gone down holding his face in the box. It was more of a shoulder to shoulder with White, and the incident is checked and cleared by VAR.

Here come two more Arsenal changes: Havertz and Lewis-Skelly deserve their ovation, replaced by Gyokeres and Zubimendi.

Chance for Tzolis to play Saka clean through on goal but he delayed a fraction and Gvardiol got back in to defend. It was a great flick on by Havertz to free Tzolis. Gyokeres is ready to replace the German.

Cherki with a shot from distance, saved by Raya. That was City’s first shot on target of the second half.

Odegaard with a disguised ball through to White, who may have been offside, and Tzolis is close to applying the touch that would have made it four. Feels like the game is meandering towards its conclusion.

Arsenal back themselves to play out from a tight spot again, but Semenyo does well to force Hincapie to concede a throw in. Arsenal then soak up another spell of City possession, they have been so much more compact defensively than Maresca’s team. Whenever Arsenal have the ball in City’s half they look dangerous, whereas City’s possession has been sterile.

City chasing shadows when Arsenal play out from the back. Arsenal moving the ball with great assurance, but you suspect everyone has an extra yard of space than they would find in a full-throttle Premier League game.

Semenyo gave Hincapie a tough time in the League Cup final in March, and was not shy in boasting about it after the game. I suspect Hincapie is a defender who keeps a little black book of those who have crossed him.

Lovely moment in midfield from Odegaard, letting the ball run across his box and pushing it beyond Rico Lewis. Saka in acres on the far side after he outmuscles Gvardiol, but he shoots into the side netting. Tried to give Donnarumma the eyes.

City with a spell of possession in the Arsenal half, and Gvardiol glances a header over the bar from a very decent Grealish cross. Arsenal hard to break down once they are in that 4-4-2 shape.

Here come the changes: Foden and Anderson off, Cherki and Rico Lewis on.

Arsenal subs: Saka and Hincapue on for Calafiori and Madueke. Saka has braids this seasons, so a new look.

Arsenal popping the ball around in the sunshine now, to olés from their fans. Maresca is about to make two more changes, so five subs before the hour tells you were City are physically. Saka is going to come on for Arsenal.

Gvardiol booked, and here come more City changes, this is a fitness exercise for Maresca now. Haaland and O’Reilly off, Marmoush and Guehi on. Arteta will surely reply in kind around the hour mark.

That really should be game over now, but given the loosey-goosey nature of these games I suppose you never know. I think the only way this fixture can matter is if one team takes a battering, and there’s a risk of that for City now.

Christos Tzolis registered 29 assists in 52 competitive games for Club Brugge last season. He’s on two assists in 48 competitive minutes for Arsenal.

What composure from the Arsenal captain, running into the box untracked and sitting down first Gvardiol then Donnarumma before finding the empty net. It is clever play from Tzolis, finding Odegaard with the pass for his second assist of the game. The run from Calafiori was important to pull City’s defence out of shape.

Take a bow, Martin Ødegaard 😮‍💨Arsenal are flying against Man City!📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/cMHbIyJ90D

Man City kick off in the second 45 minutes. These matches tend to lose their rhythm in the second half.

So far, Manchester City’s first glimpse of life after Pep Guardiola is inauspicious. Enzo Maresca might be his predecessor’s doppelgänger, but his attempt to emulate the same style has proved abortive: plenty of possession, but minimal impact. It smacks of desperation that Jack Grealish is being thrown in at half-time, his first appearance for the club for 15 months.

Looks like a pre-planned change from Manchester City and Arsenal: Jack Grealish makes an unlikely comeback, replacing Doku, and Declan Rice replaces Bruno Guimaraes. Arsenal’s two big hitters in midfield sharing the game.

7 - Kai Havertz has been involved in more goals against Manchester City (7 - 4 goals, 3 assists) than against any other side in his club career. Occasion. pic.twitter.com/ln7PQnjboJ

00:23 - Riccardo Calafiori's goal for Arsenal after 23 seconds is the first scored in the opening minute of the Community Shield since Bobby Owen for Manchester City against West Bromwich Albion in 1968.Rapid. pic.twitter.com/FCwVKuTOlh

Advantage Arsenal at half time, and they have looked a sharper, more cohesive team. City have had plenty of possession, but much of it was sterile until that late flurry when Raya saved from Haaland and White blocked Doku’s shot. The first 45 minutes will have ticked all of the boxes for Arteta: there has been some strong penalty box defending, some flowing moves from back to front and two well-taken goals.

Flimsy defending from City again, Havertz finding it easy to run to the byline, and the ball is cleared off the line after Odegaard poked the ball towards goal after a Donnarumma parry.

“You’re getting sacked in the morning,” sing the Arsenal fans at Maresca as the whistle blows.

Mosquera defends well against Doku at the expense of a corner, which Raya claims with ease. There is going to be just one minute of added time.

Arsenal playing through the pitch and City’s defensive shape again, this time it was started by a fizzed Raya pass into Tzolis. Three on three, but Madueke’s shot is straight at Donnarummma. The winger is such an outlet for his team, but the final decision is lacking too often, which is not a novel observation.

Madueke then finds White on the overlap, he chips the ball to the back post where Calafiori is free and he volleys over.

Arsenal’s defence stretched for the first time in the game. Raya saved after Haaland was picked out by Doku, with Lewis-Skelly defending well to deny a rebound, before Semenyo picks out Doku with a lofted cross, but White through himself in front of the volley and made a crucial block.

Ben White to the rescue with an incredible block 🦸📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZK0cNnFz5N

Madueke with a tame shot on goal after O’Reilly went Awol defensively, but the flag was up for offside.

Arsenal come forward again, with Havertz holding the ball up well. Tzolis reverses a pass for Calafiori, but he anticipates a challenge in the area and is rightly booked for diving.

Ben White thought he had nipped in front of Doku to intercept a straight Kovacic pass, but the referee blows for a foul against the Arsenal man.

Then Haaland has a sight of goal for the first time: a peeling run into the right channel, found by Doku, but it was tough angle on his weaker foot. Scooped it over the bar.

Foden takes up a lovely position behind the Arsenal midfield, but his through ball towards Haaland hits Gabriel on the back of the heel. Then Semenyo wins a corner in a joust with Calafiori. Referee blows for some pushing and shoving.

Eventually the corner is taken, cleared initially, before teasing Foden cross drifts beyond the back post. Foden the pick of the bunch for City, which is unsurprising considering he has a full pre-season behind him.

The Arsenal supporters are really, really enjoying this. They’re “doing the Poznan” to mock the City fans.

An ideal outing for Arsenal, so far though it can be easy to over-index these games when players are not fully match fit. But Arteta will be pleased with the fluency in the passing through midfield, which was lacking at times last season.

Christos Tzolis was signed to provide goals and assists, and he’s been doing so throughout pre-season. The Greek winger is perhaps more aggressive in his positioning than Leandro Trossard, the man he has replaced in the squad, and he was in the right place there to pick out Kai Havertz.

The new signing Tzolis is involved with a clever header back across the six-yard box, the left winger was picked out by an inswinging Odegaard cross to the back post. Havertz rose above Dias, and his header down into the turf squeezed beyond Donnarumma. The ball bounced in off the back of the goalkeeper, could well be an own goal.

Kai Havertz finishes off a well-worked move to double Arsenal's lead 🤩📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tGkxCIBV8F

Gvardiol slides across to win an important challenge when Madueke was running into space, before Odegaard fails with a scooped pass towards White.

Arsenal find Madueke in acres of space again, Bruno Guimaraes with the switch, and the winger keeps things alive despite an unconvincing dribble. Guimaraes then finds space in the box, but takes to long to pick out a man.

City soon on the attack again, and Doku runs off the back of White all too easily, but Gabriel charges in to win a booming slide tackle in the box. He greets it with his own roar of approval.

Raya claims the corner, then Foden is booked for pulling back Tzolis to stop a counter.

In these early days, long before trophies become something tangible, Mikel Arteta will want to see something far more vital than talent - hunger. It’s bursting out of Arsenal’s players, never more apparent than when Gabriel has just thundered into Jeremy Doku and celebrated the challenge like a goal. It reflective of the team’s mentality.

The passion from Gabriel after stopping Jérémy Doku 😤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/L3D8lHrBNU

City’s best moment so far: Foden with a shot from just outside the box which is pushed clear by Raya, before O’Reilly is penalised for a push on Ben White. It looked like the City man was just stronger in the shoulder to shoulder. Perhaps out frustration, O’Reilly then fouls Havertz on halfway.

The Arsenal fans massively outnumber the City supporters here, and the Londoners appear to have fallen in love with Guimaraes already. He’s snapping into tackles with real venom. There have been lots of cries of “Bruno!” in these opening 23 minutes.

Better from City, with Foden turning after receiving the ball between the lines. Then Anderson flashes a cross across the penalty area from an inside right position, but Haaland was slightly on his heels and it runs out for a goal kick.

Interesting to see Guimaraes drop all the way into Arsenal’s penalty area for their goal-kick a few minutes ago. Arsenal had massive problems playing out from the back against City in the Carabao Cup final last season. The Brazilian’s positioning could be a reaction to that.

Considering Arsenal are missing Saliba, Timber and Rice, their defence has looked relatively untroubled so far. City’s big names in attacking areas are on the pitch, but still finding their level as the new season approaches.

Arsenal have a corner after Gvardiol sticks out a leg to block Madueke’s low cross. Sharp in midfield from Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes to spread the play to the right winger. Good delivery from Madueke, headed clear, before White does well to usher the ball behind for another corner.

Gabriel and Khusanov tangle at the back post, appeals for an Arsenal penalty, but Gabriel was the first player to pull a shirt.

Gvardiol with a diagonal cross that floats behind for an Arsenal goal kick. City starting to enjoy some control in the Arsenal half, with Arteta’s team trusting their defensive shape to absorb pressure.

Arsenal with the chance to counter-attack with runners after Kovacic’s loss of possession in midfield, but Odegaard’s pass was slightly behind Madueke, who then had to check before hesitating. Surely more goals to follow, given the ease with which Arsenal are getting at City and the forward quality in Maresca’s team.

Odegaard tries a chipped pass into Havertz’s path in the penalty area but Gvardiol heads away. Moments earlier, Doku claimed he was fouled by White near the touchline but nothing doing.

Arsenal continue to flow forward, finding plenty of space in City’s half, but Tzolis’s cross deflects into the arms of Donnarumma.

There was a check for offside in the build up to Arsenal’s goal but the goal stands. Welcome back VAR, and consider the curtain raised on the new season. City enjoying some possession since conceding.

That’s certainly one way to start a new season. It’s a fabulous team goal, with Lewis-Skelly at the heart of it. There has been a lot of talk about this teenager’s future but, in this reporter’s humble opinion, it should not even be a discussion. Losing a player of this quality, a product of the club’s academy, would be a terrible mistake.

Surely the fastest goal in the history of this fixture, or most fixtures for that matter.

Arsenal were camped in City’s half from kick off, and it was superb from Lewis-Skelly in midfield to let the ball run across his body and find the run of Calafiori with a reverse pass, and the left-back keeps his cool to roll the ball beyond Donnarumma.

Riccardo Calafiori gives Arsenal the lead after just 24 seconds 🤯The assist from Myles Lewis-Skelly 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/aU0UsCB1Xs

Arsenal get the game, and the 2026-27 domestic season, started.

Former Man City player Mike Summerbee, who fans used to hail with a Small Faces-inspired chant, is involved in the preliminaries.

With no Timber, Saliba or Rice, this could be a more open game than some of the recent chess matches between these sides. The lower stakes should help with that. City have a favourable match up down their left with O’Reilly and Doku against Madueke and White. There is more ball retention in Arsenal’s team than at periods of last season, with Guimaraes, Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly and Havertz in the middle.

Sincere commiserations to the Arsenal and Manchester City supporters who have attempted to travel by road to Cardiff today. We should have nothing but sympathy for those diehards who have tried to navigate the car parks of the M5 and the M4 and nothing but scorn for whoever is in charge of planning at Wembley. Who would have thought to check the football calendar before booking a concert for the week before the new season? A total nonsense. Let’s hope the game turns out to be better than the travel.

Always a talking point during the Six Nations, but there is no reason for it to close on a sunny afternoon on the banks of the River Taff. That will mean a slightly annoying shadow across the pitch, always a potential irritant in these August or May showpieces.

I said already in the last days, no matter if we are in August or May, it is a final and when it is a final we need to win.

[Players coming back from the World Cup] Many, many players, for us for them, we are in the exact same situation. It depends how we can manage the game, we will see.

[What he expects from Anderson] Exactly the player he is. We are not asking him something more. He is a good player on and off the ball, always making an effort for his team-mates.

I said in the press conference, we are going to decide the four captains when the window closes. At the moments, Ruben Dias and Erling are with us [no comment on Rodri’s future].

Good afternoon from Cardiff, where the sun is shining and the fans are enjoying the pubs outside the Principality Stadium. The teams are allowed nine substitutes today, which has really highlighted the bloated nature of Arsenal’s squad. There’s no space for Ethan Nwaneri, Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus, Fabio Vieira or Reiss Nelson. All five of them could be sold by the end of the month.

I had plenty of rest, some work as well, it was a break that I really enjoyed.

Very much [on if he was impressed with his signings]. Christos [Tzolis] came early which always helps with a new signing, and Bruno joined us last week after a long summer with him but he is in good condition.

I think it is something very individual. [Declan] Rice played more than 65 games, he needed a complete rest and we need to build him. It’s not only physical, it’s mental freshness. For the players not involved in the World Cup it is a bit different. They remain so competitive. They wanted to be involved and that’s good to see as well.

[On Bruno] He is a ball of energy. He has an unbelievable desire to win every ball. You sense he will drive the dressing room and when you bring someone with that competitive nature, it will only drive the boys.

[On retaining the title] Still recognise the big margins that we have to improve as a team, individually and as well the ambition of the club which is unquestionable.

Elliot Anderson makes his first City appearance, and he will be partnered by Mateo Kovacic in midfield with Nico O’Reilly drifting into those areas from midfield. Phil Foden, who did not go to the World Cup, starts ahead of Rayan Cherki and Doku, Haaland and Semenyo is City’s strongest front three. No Rodri, but Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Man City starting XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O’Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson; Semenyo, Foden, Doku; Haaland

Subs: Rulli, Guéhi, Marmoush, Cherki, Nico, Grealish, Aït-Nouri, Nunes, Lewis

The other interesting snippets are Arteta plumping for Madueke over Max Dowman on the right, Havertz over Gyokeres and Calafiori over Hincapie. Also worth noting that there is no place in the squad for Ethan Nwaneri nor Gabriel Martinelli who have been linked with moves. The same goes for Fabio Vieira, Gabriel Jesus and Reiss Nelson.

Arsenal starting XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Lewis-Skelly, Odegaard; Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis

Subs: Kepa, Hincapie, Rice, Zubimendi, Merino, Eze, Dowman, Saka, Gyokeres

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Mikel names a strong starting XI 👊🤝Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/bckDyMazRo

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka are with the group, but they have not kicked a ball in pre-season. They are looking at half hour of football at the absolute maximum today.

In case any Arsenal fan had forgotten that last season ended with them losing a Champions League final on penalties, City fans are on hand to remind them. They have one European Cup to Arsenal’s zero. Away from the tin foil trophies, I’m sure much bottle-related mirth is on the cards, especially now broadcasters and fans are aware of the viral possibilities. Too aware, I would argue.

The pool of players who can improve the Premier League champions and Champions League finalists is a small one, but it is still fair to point out that Arsenal’s summer has not gone smoothly. They pursued Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior without success, and Arteta’s desire to take the team to a “different dimension” has so far gone unfulfilled., certainly in the forward positions.

Arsenal still look strong, but have they passed up a chance to pull away from the rest? Sam Wallace takes a look at their summer so far.

It would have been less stressful for Guardiola to go once he realised the great side of Kevin De Bruyne was nearing its end. Instead he opted to oversee a rebuild that gives his successor a greater chance of immediate success, going close to the title last season in what was effectively year one for a re-emerging City side. Guardiola must have known he was signing Gianluigi Donnarumma, Antoine Semenyo, Marc Guéhi and Rayan Cherki for someone else’s long-term benefit.

The Community Shield returns to Cardiff’s Principality Stadium for the first time since 2006, and a different dynamic is at play between Arsenal and Manchester City.

When the two clubs played at Wembley in this fixture three years ago, it felt like a more significant occasion for Arsenal as they sought to prove that the gap was closing to Pep Guardiola’s champions.

Now it is Arsenal and Mikel Arteta who have a league title behind them, while Enzo Maresca is the manager hoping to build credibility as City turn the page post-Pep Guardiola.

In truth, these two teams will look very different by the time the season gathers pace in autumn. World Cup exertions mean Elliot Anderson, Erling Haaland, Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka will be minimally involved in this game, while transfer plans remain up in the air for both camps.

City appear bound to lose Rodri, in addition to Bernardo Silva and Tijjani Reijnders in central midfield. Rodri’s sale would expedite a move for Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, and possibly Enzo Fernandez despite Chelsea’s insistence that the deadline to sign him for £120m has passed.

Arsenal are also open for business, hoping to add a right-sided defender to help them cope with William Saliba’s absence. The £75m purchase of Bruno Guimarães means the champions’ midfield options look formidable, but so far it has been another summer without a level-raising forward signing. Christos Tzolis in and Leandro Trossard out looks canny business, but falls into the category of like for like.

Although Arsenal held their nerve to see off City in the title race, they failed to win in three attempts against their rivals, including a limp defeat in the Carabao Cup final at Wembley. Arsenal also failed to win, or score, against Liverpool in the Premier League last season so their record in the big games is an area for improvement.

The victors this afternoon will claim to have laid a marker down, the losers will write the game off as a warm up exercise.

#1679. Nottingham Forest vs. Chelsea: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Premier League clash

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 13:37

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will attempt to earn a much-needed boost in the Premier League when they square off on Friday night.

Despite seven points separating these teams in the Premier League table, the home side are arguably the favourites to prevail from this fixture.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Premier League match will kick off at 8pm, UK time, on Saturday.

This Premier League game between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea will be held at the City Ground, the home stadium of Forest.

Last season's corresponding fixture ended in a 3-0 victory for Chelsea, albeit in a game where Forest - then with Ange Postecoglou at the helm - squandered a number of opportunities.

The Premier League contest will be available on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League for viewers in the UK.

Sky customers can access the Premier League match on Sky Go and on the Sky Sports app, while it is also available via Now TV's Sports membership.

Sky Sports will show highlights, including any goals which have been scored, on their social media and YouTube channels, as well as on their dedicated app.

Meanwhile, those wishing to watch highlights on Match of the Day will have to wait until Saturday evening, with the programme starting at 10.30pm.

Both teams head into this fixture with question marks over their physicality, an issue which Oliver Glasner addressed in his pre-match press conference.

Forest begin the latest batch of games sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, but they can move into 14th place with victory on Friday night.

Eight teams - including Chelsea - possess a worse defensive record than Forest, emphasising the feeling that they could quickly move up the standings if they resolve their issues in the final third.

On the back of three defeats in four matches and with 20 goals conceded in 11 games, Chelsea will be perceived to be ideal opponents for Forest.

While Chelsea have the opportunity to move into fifth place, they are highly likely to end the weekend in the bottom half of the table should they lose in the East Midlands.

#1678. Liverpool FC: Klopp Won’t Buy Big In January, & Why It’s The Right Move

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool FC: Klopp Won't Buy Big In January, & Why It's The Right Move

Jurgen Kloppai??i??s countrymen are well versed with the appeal of quick fixes. They once allowed one of historyai??i??s most hated figures to rise to power. Of course, when Adolf Hitler was rapidly gaining popularity in Germany, he didnai??i??t do it by telling his people he would bring about the Second World War so soon after the first one had concluded. No, he did it by promising quick fixes. In a country reeling from the effects of the first World War and later the onset of the Great Depression, the promises of a party that would swoop in and fix issues ranging from more practical ones like unemployment, to rather more emotional ones like the loss of national pride after the defeat in the previous World War, was welcome to the masses.

Liverpool FC is a little like post World War I Germany — a lot of pride, but very little recent success to validate all that ego. As a result, the fans are in a constant state of impatience, always hoping the next player or the next manager will be the one to lead them back to the glory days. Thereai??i??s nothing wrong with having hope, but it needs to be balanced with practicality. Overly inflated expectations almost always tend to blow up in oneai??i??s face.

Jurgen Klopp is quite different from the former Nazi party leader of course. From day 1, heai??i??s been trying to temper expectations rather than fuel them.

a Expectations can be a really big problem. Itai??i??s like a backpack ai??i?? 20 kilos more! Iai??i??m not here to promise that against Tottenham you will see the new LFC, but maybe some of it. Everything in life takes time, the only thing nobody gives time is development.a ai??i?? Jurgen Klopp

Instead itai??i??s the fans that are overburdening the manager and the team with their dreams of an overnight turnover of fortunes. With every 4-1 against Manchester City and 6-1 rout over Southampton, the fans have responded by hailing their players footballing maestros, and their manager a genius. When these games have been inevitably followed by underwhelming performances, the same players have been declared a Brendan Rodgersai??i?? signingsa and a not worthy of wearing a Liverpool shirta . Neither of these stands is right, and there is a dire need for fans to ground themselves in reality, and really understand where the club stands.

Insanity is doing the same things over and over again and expecting different results. In the past, Liverpool have conducted mass-recruitment, spending a pretty penny in the process, and not really seen any major reversal of fortunes. So now that results have been poor in recent weeks, what do fans want? New signings of course. Ignoring the fact that squad overhauls havenai??i??t helped in the past. And ignoring the fact that Klopp does not generally delve deeply into the scouting process, hence the transfer committee is likely to be just as influential as it was during Brendan Rodgersai??i?? tenure (if not more).

The good news is that Jurgen Klopp seems far from keen to jump onto the transfer bandwagon. Heai??i??s instead decided to focus on the rich pool of players already on the teamai??i??s rolls, either on loan to other clubs or playing for the youth club. This greatly reflects his vision and ability to curb any impulse to seek a ready-made answer in the transfer market.

If you include the loan and youth players, Liverpoolai??i??s squad strength is pretty massive. So there is little sense in buying loads of new players, unless thereai??i??s conclusive evidence that the current crop canai??i??t cut it at the highest level. Seeing how itai??i??s still early days in the reign of Klopp, itai??i??s unlikely he would have been able to reach that conclusion about too many of his players.

In the last two weeks, Klopp has recalled loanees Tiago Ilori (Aston Villa), Sheyi Ojo (Wolverhampton), Ryan Kent (Coventry City), Danny Ward (Aberdeen) and Kevin Stewart (Swindon Town). Against Exeter City, he also utilized all of these players barring Ward, and played youngsters Cameron Brannagan, Joao Carlos Teixeira, Jerome Sinclair, Brad Smith and Connor Randall.

This is exactly what the youth academy is there for, and itai??i??s very pleasing to see Klopp isnai??i??t ignoring it and focusing on the transfer market. That being said, itai??i??s not as if the German should never sign a player. In the transfer market, there are 3 types of signings — the doai??i??s, the donai??i??ts, and the ones you sign only if you absolutely have to.

So then, thereai??i??s only two possible types of players Liverpool should be buying in the winter window:

In the summer windows, one can look at options beyond these two. Your scouting team can have a list of targets, clubs are more open to listening to offers, and you have an opportunity to move out some of your own players to make room for signings. You also have a solid pre-season ahead, so that players who might need to be brought up to speed on the teamai??i??s style of play can be worked with before theyai??i??re thrown into the deep end. January simply isnai??i??t the right time for all this.

So what kind of signings should be avoided? Letai??i??s just call them the a Southampton signingsai??i??. These are the so-called a Premier League readyai??i?? players who seem like an improved version of the current squad, mostly based on their performances in the current season. Some examples of such players would be the likes of Saido Mane, Marko Arnautovic, and Riyad Mahrez. All 3 are talented players, and on paper would make good additions to a side that has not performed well in front of goal. But one good season does not a good player make. Keep in mind that Christian Benteke, Adam Lallana, Dejan Lovren and Roberto Firmino were all their former clubsai??i?? best players, and highly coveted at the time, but none of them have been instant hits at Merseyside. Therefore, to imagine that a January signing will suddenly improve your season is misguided, and you end up paying over the odds as most clubs donai??i??t want to lose their best players mid-way through the season.

One recent transfer rumour has linked Alexandre Pato to a move to Merseyside. What a pointless and risky transfer this would be. Liverpool already have 4 senior strikers on their rolls, excluding Roberto Firmino who can also play up front. Other than Daniel Sturridge, who is one day elder to Pato, all the other 3 are younger than the Brazilian. Before his move to the Brazilian league, his injury record at AC Milan was as bad as Daniel Sturridgeai??i??s. All 4 of the Liverpool forwards have proven themselves either in the Premier League (Ings, Sturridge, Benteke) or the French Ligue 1 (Origi).

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1677. Europa League preview: Olympiacos vs. AC Milan – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

AC Milan will make the trip to Greece with the hopes of turning a corner against Olympiacos after a rough start to their Europa League campaign.

It has been a tale of two competitions this season so far for Milan. In Serie A they are inside the top four and have won eight games out of 12, leading to suggestions of a Scudetto bid. However, in Europe they have lost three of four, and sit in the bottom eight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It means that they’ll have to be perfect to even be in with a chance of a top eight finish – given you’ve needed at least 15 points in the last two seasons. Nevertheless, a point and gaining a bit of momentum across all competitions would still be appreciated.

Game date: Thursday, November 26 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: Karaiskakis Stadium Referee: Chris Kavanagh (VAR: Bankes)

As mentioned, things have been going quite well for Milan domestically. Sunday’s 5-1 victory against surprise package Frosinone was another example of the potential of this team, but there remains a necessity to find some consistency.

This is especially the case when it comes to the Europa League, in which the Rossoneri have been quire frankly awful. A 4-0 win against RB Salzburg in round two was the only glimmer of light, with the other three games being defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring.

As things stand right now, Milan would not even make the play-off spots as they sit outside the top 24. There is only one point in it and even eighth is only four points away, though the runway is getting shorter with only 12 points to play for.

The result of this is that Amorim is expected to name quite a strong side for the game, but we must start with the injury absences. The big doubt is Strahinja Pavlovic, who needs another check on a kidney stone problem despite playing 20 minutes off the bench against Frosinone.

Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano and Ruben Loftus-Cheek have all missed the past few games due to various issues and will not be available on Thursday either.

On Tuesday, the news broke that Milan will be without Luka Modric, who felt a tweak in his right thigh during the last game. The Croatian will be given Thursday night to recover and potentially the Cagliari game too, with the hopes of having him back at the start of December. Then, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi have already been ruled out.

The other bit of news is that Fikayo Tomori returned to training on Wednesday, which is a big boost given how thin the options are in defence, but it remains to be seen if the Englishman is deemed fit enough to play a part after his absence.

With the squad running quite thin, Amorim won’t have many options to rotate, nor does he have the luxury to with the standings.

Nevertheless, there will be one at the back, where Pervis Estupinan is expected to start. Mike Maignan starts behind Sankhoun Diawara and Koni De Winter, with Mario Gila at right-back again.

Modric’s injury means Ardon Jashari will be given a chance on Thursday, and it’s one he must take. Alongside him, he’ll be covered with reliability from Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot, which should help.

Finally, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are expected to start on the flanks, with Goncalo Ramos through the middle.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Bouyer, Torriani, F. Terracciano, M. Cissé, Tomori, Perera, Comotto, Vos, Ossola, Hutchinson, Cisse, Menon

Injuries & suspensions: Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Modric, Pavlovic, Camarda, Bartesaghi

Olympiacos came into the new season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

In the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

The spending was almost totally offset by four big sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

Mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

Olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

In the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

In terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey may be the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

In defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical issues, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

AC Milan and Olympiacos have faced each other four times. Two came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19, which means that the meetings were almost 60 years apart.

In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

The most recent encounters were eight years ago as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

Starting in midfield, the obvious choice here is Ardon Jashari. This has been called his game by the Italian media and it’s tough to disagree. If he’s going to have a future with the club beyond this season, a strong start tomorrow is imperative.

The other obvious choice is Pervis Estupinan. The Ecuadorian is a late entry into the expected XI, despite reports linking him with a potential exit in January. Bartesaghi’s injury means he’ll be given a chance and maybe, just maybe, it’s not too late for him. Something of promise needs to be seen, though.

With Milan lacking Modric in their midfield, it could allow someone like Remo Freuler to take the game by his pace. He’s got plenty of European experience and with the Rossoneri likely to rely on Jashari to set the pace, he may take the edge.

Then, if Leon Bailey starts, he’ll be the big threat of the night. Facing Estupinan and Diawara, he’ll have the opportunity to face a duo that have no relation yet. If he catches them out, it could be a long night for the Diavolo.

It’s been a real case of Jekyll and Hyde for Milan in the Europa League, to the point where it’s tough to call which side we’ll see. Logically, after such a heavy win at the weekend, the visitors should be coming away with three points.

However, both teams aren’t brilliant defensively and it could become an open game as a result. Considering what’s at stake, though, the Rossoneri may just edge past the hosts, but it won’t be easy…

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

The Opta supercomputer has delivered its match predictions ahead of another weekend of the 2026-27 Premier League season.

The top three all dropped points last weekend, with Arsenal and Manchester City drawing with Newcastle United and Fulham, and Brighton stunned by two stoppage-time goals from Hull City.

Liverpool took advantage of that to close the gap with their 4-0 thrashing of 10-man Manchester United – with Mauricio Pochettino's disappointing start seeing the Red Devils stay in the bottom three.

Thomas Frank also got off to a losing start at Crystal Palace, who remain bottom of the table, after a 3-2 loss to Coventry City in his first game.

Matchday 12 sees fixtures take place across Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Ahead of what should be another intriguing set of Premier League games, let's check out the Opta supercomputer’s match predictions.

The weekend kicks off at the City Ground on Friday, with Nottingham Forest and Chelsea both looking to get back to winning ways.

Since the start of March, no side has lost more Premier League games than Chelsea (13), who were beaten by Sunderland and Leeds United in their last two outings. Similarly, among ever-present sides, only Crystal Palace (17) have earned fewer points than the Blues (23) over the same period.

Chelsea are at least unbeaten in their last five away league games against Forest (W4 D1), winning each of the last three, though our predictive model gives them just a 33.5% chance of stretching that run to four.

Forest, who won 39.9% of the pre-match simulations, are looking to win consecutive league games against Chelsea for the first time since April 1979, though there is also a 26.6% chance of a draw.

#1675. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1673. Frosinone vs Parma - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 26 Nov 2026 13:47

Both beaten 5-1 last weekend, Frosinone and Parma will aim to bounce back when they clash at Stadio Benito Stirpe on Saturday.

Despite suffering consecutive defeats for the first time this term, the hosts are still 12 points above their visitors in the Serie A standings.

Frosinone made an unexpectedly strong start to their latest comeback campaign, scoring freely while winning six of their first 11 fixtures after returning to Serie A.

However, Massimiliano Alvini's attack-minded side then suffered a rare setback, going down 1-0 to Cagliari, before they were well beaten just after the international break.

Two goals down within 20 minutes, the Canarini continued to fly forward, but they never really recovered and ultimately lost 5-1 to AC Milan at San Siro.

In fact, Frosinone have only claimed two points on the road since beating Fiorentina at the end of August, so their form at Stadio Stirpe has kept them tucked inside the top half.

After narrowly losing their first home fixture against Juventus, they have since won all of the next five, so confidence should still be high when lowly Parma come to town.

While their promoted hosts sit seventh in Serie A, Parma are hovering above the relegation zone with just eight points on the board.

Like Frosinone, they were thumped 5-1 last week, as Roma stormed to victory at Stadio Tardini, with Capocannoniere leader Donyell Malen helping himself to four goals.

That was the Gialloblu's eighth defeat from their first 12 league games, and the recent hiring of their second-highest Serie A scorer has hardly had an impact.

Alberto Gilardino has only celebrated one win since succeeding Carlos Cuesta, who kept the Emilian club afloat last term, but that lone success did come on the road.

Following a run of six straight away defeats, Parma recently beat Atalanta 3-0 in Bergamo, so they will aim to claim more points when they head south on Saturday.

Now trailing Malen in the race to be crowned Italy's top scorer, Frosinone striker Antonio Raimondo is still sidelined by injury - and his deputy is also unavailable.

Daniel Birligea bagged a brace against Lecce before scoring for Romania in their recent Nations League camp, but he strained a hamstring in Milan and has been ruled out for the next few weeks.

So, it remains to be seen whether Alvini selects support forwards Fares Ghedjemis, Romano Schmid and Giorgi Kvernadze - each of whom have provided four Serie A assists - or Slovak centre-forward Tomas Bobcek to lead the hosts' attack.

On the absence front, Florian Grillitsch has yet to recover from a thigh problem, but left-back Gabriele Bracaglia can return after serving a one-match ban.

While Parma will welcome back Abdoulaye Ndiaye from suspension, Argentine striker David Romero is still ruled out by a serious shoulder injury; defensive duo Diego Carlos (thigh) and Dominik Drobnic (foot) are also doubts.

In Romero's absence, Simone Lontani could partner El Bilal Toure, but Nesta Elphege is also a contender after scoring the Gialloblu's lone goal against Roma.

Palmisani; Oyono, Monterisi, Calvani, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek

Daffara; Delprato, Troilo, Ndiaye; Britschgi, Fabbian, Sierro, Keita, Valeri; Elphege, Toure

Frosinone can arrest their decline with another home win, as Parma are in grim form and could face a long fight to avoid the drop.

Notably, the Canarini tend to start fast - scoring a league-high 11 goals inside the first 30 minutes - while their visitors have yet to score before the half-hour mark.

#1672. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1671. Marmoush backs Spurs youngster Williams-Barnett to have ‘very big future’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Omar Marmoush has backed his "unbelievable" Tottenham team-mate Luca Williams-Barnett to have a "very big future".

The teenager has impressed under Roberto De Zerbi in recent weeks, most notably scoring and assisting in their Premier League win over Ipswich Town last weekend.

Aged 18 years and 51 days, Williams-Barnett became the second-youngest player to score and assist in a Premier League game, behind Michael Owen.

He also became the fourth-youngest player to score on his first Premier League start, behind Daniel Jebbison in May 2021 (17y 276d), Danny Cadamarteri in September 1997 (17y 343d) and Mark Cullen in May 2010 (18y 12d).

Should he start and score against Sunderland on Sunday, he'd be the youngest player to score in his first two starts (18 years, 59 days).

The forward's breakthrough into the Spurs' first team was rewarded with a new contract, which is reported to be a five-year deal, and Marmoush believes the only way is up for the exciting winger.

"He is unbelievable," Marmoush told Sky sports about Williams-Barnett.

It's always been Tottenham. https://t.co/W3mx3ZQIH9

— Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) November 24, 2026

"He is a great, great talent and what I like most about him, of course, his talent is something that everyone sees, is that he is very brave, too.

"And when he came on in his first game, he just took the ball and tried things. He is very direct, tries to beat his opponent and he has a very, very promising future ahead of him.

"He has got it, and you can see that. One of the big traits of a big talent, and a big player, is the personality and the character and that is what stands out most for me, his courage and to be brave.

"As a young lad, to come into Spurs' first team and perform like that is not easy, and just to believe in yourself and do the actions on your pitch is great.

"I hope he is enjoying it, and he will have a very, very big future, that's for sure."
